+# CamCraft 0.25.0 (clean-room implementation)
+
+Released 2026-11-22.
+
+## Breaking
+This release has breaking changes. **The project file format goes from
+version 69 to 75.** 0.25.0 opens the files of 0.24.0 and older: a file of
+an older version steps up and keeps its content. 0.24.0 and older builds
+refuse a file that 0.25.0 saves.
+- **Sketch selections need format 74** (#1864, PR #2716; #1868, PR #2920).
+  2D Contour, Slot and Trochoidal Slot can read picked DXF sketch chains and
+  layers, with a side and a direction for each chain. A project with such
+  picks is saved as format 74 or later. A v73 file steps up unchanged.
+- **Machine installation facts need format 75** (#3181, PR #3204). A machine
+  can record its installed control, the exact NC software, the installed
+  options and the tool-change procedure. Older readers refuse such a file,
+  so that a save in an older build cannot lose these facts. A v74 file steps
+  up with these facts not stated.
+- The other format steps of this release:
+  - v70: a tool's library holder is a reference to the holder library
+    entry, not a drawn copy (#2016, PR #2092). Tool library files
+    (`.camtools`) go to version 4.
+  - v71: a DXF profile can be placed on the stock of a setup (#1862,
+    PR #2134).
+  - v72: a model can be linked to its source file and is imported again
+    when the file changes (#2463, PR #2563).
+  - v73: "Do not touch" face and edge protection on clearing operations
+    (#2055, PR #2149, merged through PR #2704).
+- A stock copy of an incomplete model keeps the name of its source model's
+  hole after the source is deleted (#1700, PR #2024). Such a project file
+  does not open in 0.21.0 to 0.24.0.
+
+A minor release headlined by **DXF sketches as operation geometry** (2D
+Contour, Slot, Trochoidal Slot, Wire Contour, typed engraving text),
+**first-traverse checks for every operation kind and machine layout**,
+**STEP import through the solidcore kernel only**, **new posts** (Heidenhain
+iTNC 530 Klartext, Grbl 1.1, LinuxCNC 3-axis), **a Slot Undercut
+operation**, **fine boring (G76)**, **dogbone and T-bone corner relief**,
+**AI chat with provider clients and context budgets**, and **a Home page**.
+259 pull requests merged since 0.24.0 (50 features, 162 fixes, 3
+performance changes, 1 refactor, docs, tests and process).
+
+## Upgrade notes
+- Save a project in 0.25.0 only when each person who opens it also has
+  0.25.0. Older builds refuse format 75 (see "Breaking").
+- STEP files are now read only through the solidcore kernel. The truck STEP
+  crates are removed (#917, PR #2904; PR #2939). Faulty STEP files are
+  refused by name, and touching solids import as separate bodies. A model
+  can import with different facets than in 0.24.0. Generate and verify old
+  jobs again before you post them.
+- More programs are refused before the post (see "Changes to posted
+  G-code"). A first rapid that can hit the stock, a fixture or the table now
+  holds the post by name. Raise the clearance height as the message says.
+- Drill and thread operations take the lower of the tool feed and the
+  material feed. A feed above the tool feed holds the post (#2598, #2724).
+- A project that an older build saved after a tilt angle edit on a pre-v65
+  operation can keep the old plane basis (#2739, PR #2751). Change Tool axis
+  A or B, set it back, and check the preview before you post.
+- FreeBSD is no longer a supported platform (#2570).
+
+## Changes to posted G-code
+These change the program that an existing project posts, or stop a post that
+went through before.
+- **New posts:** Heidenhain iTNC 530 Klartext for the Fehlmann Picomax 55
+  (#3182), Grbl 1.1 for 3-axis mills (#2481), a generic LinuxCNC 3-axis
+  mill post (#2303), and a zero-step Agie punch setup encoder (#2984).
+- **The first traverse after a tool change is judged** for 3+2 planes, cross
+  drills, rotary, multi-axis and mill kinds, on mills, lathes and mill-turns,
+  through every pose of the work-turning rotaries (#2965, #2987, #2991,
+  #3077, #3081, #3083, #3084, #3096, #3100, #3127). The opening rapid starts
+  over the entry point of the operation, not over the WCS origin (#2901).
+- **Drilling:** a fine boring cycle (G76 on Haas; other posts refuse it by

-## #1198 - Viewport bar snapping and typed values (slice d)
-
-**What was decided.**
-- **Expand the bottom overlay bar upward only when Move or Rotate mode is
-  active.** When neither handle mode is on, the bar remains the 12-button
-  strip (`bar_rect`, 368 x 38 px), keeping the default shell layout and pixel
-  snapshots unchanged. When Move or Rotate is on, the same rounded grey
-  background extends upward by one compact control strip (`panel_rect`,
-  368 x 66 px) hosting the axis selector (`X`, `Y`, `Z`), the typed distance
-  or angle field (`TextEdit` + `Set` / Enter), and the snap step parameter.
-  `viewcube::Hud::contains` covers the full expanded bar so clicks and drags
-  on those widgets never start viewport orbit or picking, and
-  `viewport_layout::furniture_with_bar` lifts the legend and empty-document
-  line above the expanded height.
-- **Hold Shift to snap; defaults are 1.0 mm (Move) and 90.0 degrees
-  (Rotate).** `BodyDrag` and `TurnDrag` track the unsnapped raw drag
-  (`raw_delta`, `raw_angle`) separately from the active previewed/released
-  value (`delta`, `angle`) so pressing or releasing Shift mid-drag toggles
-  snapping smoothly without accumulation drift. Both snap parameters are
-  positive bounded fields in the bar (`0.001..=10_000.0` mm through the active
-  unit lens, `0.1..=360.0` degrees), and `DEFAULT_ROTATE_SNAP_DEG = 90.0`
-  matches the 90-degree requirement in #1198 while remaining editable in the
-  bar for finer angles such as 15 or 45 degrees.
-- **Typed entry applies through the existing drag commands.** Typing a
-  distance or angle in the bar and pressing Enter or clicking `Set` converts
-  from the active display unit (`units::from_display`) or degrees to radians,
-  refuses non-finite / missing-selection inputs by name, skips zero-length
-  deltas with no history step, and queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy` or
-  `CommandKind::TurnModelBy` — so undo, staleness, following stock and
-  aligned-setup frames work identically to dragging a handle.
-
-**Why.**
-- Keeping the control strip hidden while Move and Rotate are off avoids
-  unrequested bar clutter in normal navigation and avoids changing the
-  default shell width (`viewcube::min_width`) or default pixel goldens.
-- Using `Shift` for handle snapping avoids colliding with `Ctrl`/`Cmd`
-  shortcuts and `Alt` window-manager drags on Linux.
-- Reusing `MoveModelBy` / `TurnModelBy` preserves one command path (`MoveModel`)
-  and requires no new app command or MCP tool.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-- **Always showing snap and value widgets in the main bar:** dropped because
-  the inputs are mode-specific (mm/in distance vs degree angle) and widening
-  the base bar would crowd narrow panes and shift every resting viewport
-  golden.
-- **Persisting snap steps in per-user `prefs.json`:** dropped to match the
-  other viewport-bar toggles (`move_handles`, `rotate_handles`, `pick_through`),
-  which are session view state in `crates/ui` and require no app preference
-  format changes.
-- **Using `DragValue` instead of `TextEdit` for the typed move/turn input:**
-  dropped because `DragValue` fires `changed()` on intermediate keystrokes
-  and silently discards invalid text, whereas `TextEdit` + `Set` / `Enter`
-  commits exactly one command on submit and refuses non-finite text by name.
-
-**Cost to change later.**
-Low and local to `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_controls.rs`,
-`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs` and `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs`. Changing the
-default snap steps, adding prefs persistence, or moving the controls onto a
-combined move+rotate gizmo (#2624) touches only those UI fields and helpers.

-# 1339 - Vouch for a mesh of unknown fidelity
-
-Issue: #1339 (a follow-up of #1056).
-
-## What was chosen
-
-- A new undoable command, `VouchModelFidelity { model, by }`. It clears the
-  "fidelity unknown" mark (`model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`) of one model and of
-  the stocks copied straight from it. Undo puts each mark back.
-- The command applies to the unknown sentinel only. It refuses by name:
-  - a model with a recorded coarse chord (#864);
-  - an incomplete model (#1610, a mesh with a hole);
-  - a model that is not marked;
-  - a name that is not a model;
-  - an empty name of the person who vouches.
-- The record of who vouched is a new component, `FidelityVouched { by, rev }`.
-  `rev` is the geometry revision of the model at the time of the vouch.
-- The record speaks only while the model has that revision and no fidelity
-  flag (`model_vouch::by_of`). An import, an update or a repair lands other
-  facets, and the record is then silent. No other command changes for this.
-- The history names who vouched. `VouchModelFidelity::run` executes the
-  command as one labelled undo group (`History::top_label`). It also logs
-  the vouch at `info` level.
-- The project file keeps the record in the optional key `fidelity_vouched`
-  of the model row. The loader refuses the key on a row that is not a
-  model, beside a fidelity flag, or with an empty name.
-- The MCP tool is `vouch_model_fidelity { model, by }`. `get_job` shows
-  `fidelity_vouched` on the model. Scripts use the tool through
-  `cam.call("vouch_model_fidelity", ...)`, which is the script seam for
-  each undoable MCP tool (#2393).
-- The model page shows a name field and the button "Vouch for this mesh"
-  below the "Fidelity unknown" line. A vouched model shows who vouched.
-
-## Why
-
-- A recorded chord is a measurement. A hole is a fact about the mesh. The
-  word of a person does not replace either, so the command refuses them.
-- The gate refuses each operation on an unknown mesh, and the laws read
-  that mesh untightened at generation. The toolpaths that exist are thus
-  the toolpaths of an exact mesh. The command regenerates nothing.
-- The revision in the record keeps a stale vouch silent with no edit to
-  `UpdateModel`, `RepairModel` or `ImportModel`. Open PR #2024 changes
-  those files, so this also prevents a conflict.
-
-## What was dropped
-
-- No project version step. An old reader that drops `fidelity_vouched`
-  loads the same unmarked model and loses only the name, as with
-  `mesh_open`. The gate result is the same.
-- No change to `UNKNOWN_NOTE`. The refusal text still says to re-import the
-  model. Many tests pin that text. The model page and the MCP tool
-  description tell the user about the vouch.
-- No vouch for a stock copy whose source model is deleted. The command
-  takes a model name. Such a stock still needs a new stock definition.
-- No vouch through a chain of copies. Only a stock copied straight from the
-  model, with the unknown mark of its own, is cleared. A copy with a
-  recorded chord keeps it.
-- No identity check of `by`. The application has no user accounts. The
-  name is plain text that the person types.
-- No dedicated script verb. `cam.call` is the seam.

-## #1444 - Slot Undercut: T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop passes that never move in Z under material
-
-**What was decided**
-
-1. **Four cutter kinds, no new tool fields.** `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, `Dovetail`
-   and `Lollipop` join `ToolKind` (file words `t_slot`, `keyseat`,
-   `dovetail`, `lollipop`; additive, no `PROJECT_VERSION` step). They read
-   the existing fields: `diameter` is the head, `flute_len` the head's
-   height, `shank_d` / `shank_len` the neck, `tip_angle` the dovetail's
-   flank angle off the bottom face. One reading for every consumer:
-   `camcraft_tools::undercut::Undercut` (head shape, neck radius, contact
-   point).
-2. **One operation kind, `Slot Undercut`** (`OpParams::SlotUndercut`, tag
-   44, appended). The centre line is typed: `a`, `b` and a DXF-style
-   `bulge` (0 = straight, else a circular arc). The undercut `width` is
-   measured at the cutter's widest point, so the pass offset comes from
-   the profile's contact radius, not from the tip.
-3. **The Z law is a construction law and a verified law.** The generator
-   changes Z at one XY station only (`run_in` behind `a` on the entry
-   tangent) and checks that on the built path. The verifier has a new
-   mode (`Mode::Undercut`) and law (g): any move that changes Z while
-   material stands in or over the head's disc is `Warning::UndercutLift`
-   (blocking); a neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a
-   `ShankHit`. Both are re-read against the stock the program ahead left
-   (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`), so a neck slot or an entry pocket that an
-   earlier operation cut is air. With no such cut the conviction stands.
-4. **An undercut clears no column.** In `Mode::Undercut` the verifier's
-   rest model takes no cut from the path, and the column stock engines
-   (program verdict, carried stock, rest grids) remove nothing for an
-   undercut operation. A column holds one top per (x, y): lowering it to
-   the head would remove the roof and report a false gouge, and would let
-   a lift through the roof pass as a retract in its own kerf.
-5. **The true profile where a solid can hold it.** The solid law judges
-   head and neck against the part mesh with the real head: `Prof::Dove`
-   (frustum) and `Prof::Ball` (whole ball) beside the existing disc. The
-   field stock (`Stock::simulate_undercut`) removes the head and the neck
-   as two convex solids (their union is the non-convex cutter), with a new
-   exact frustum solid (`SdfTool::Dovetail`). The stock view uses it.
-6. **Refusal instead of support where nothing is verified:** a flipped WCS
-   and a rotated work offset refuse the kind; an aligned setup and a WCS
-   yaw do not list it (refused by their own doors); no 3+2 tilt.
-7. **A cylinder against a 'Do not touch' item** (merge of main, #2055).
-   Main's avoid law grows each atom by the clearance
-   (`swept::rho_expanded`). For `Prof::Dove` and `Prof::Ball` it reads the
-   circumscribed cylinder: the head's largest radius over the atom's
-   height. `avoid_poly` stretches an atom over a Z range, and a profile
-   that is not non-decreasing would then report too small a radius above
-   its bottom. The cylinder holds the head at each stretch, so the law
-   can refuse a legal move near a protected item by at most the head's
-   taper, and never passes a violation. The stretched atom has no `cap`
-   allowance: a protected item is never cut. *Dropped:* the exact grown
-   frustum and ball, which are correct only for an atom that is not
-   stretched and need a second code path for the keep-out.
-   Pinned by `crates/sim/tests/verify_avoid_undercut.rs`.
-
-**Why**
-
-- The issue's safety statement is about Z moves under material. A plain
-  contour's laws read a vertical retract as "rides its own kerf", which is
-  false under a roof. The law had to say so in the verifier, not only in
-  the generator, because a path can be edited, pasted or produced by a
-  later generator.
-- Reusing `shank_d` as the neck keeps every existing reader of the tool
-  record correct: `Tool::profile`, the drawn-cutter law and the verifier's
-  shank band already describe "a cylinder head on a narrower shank". Only
-  the dovetail and the ball needed new profile code.
-- A union of convex solids keeps the field engine's convex sweep law
-  (golden section on a convex distance) true for each piece. A general
-  non-convex revolved profile would need a bracketed search (issue 896's
-  research, slice 2) and was not needed for these four heads.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- *A generic `FormMill` kind with a drawn outline* (issue 896, slice 1).
-  It needs the drawn outline to survive `cutter_fit::refit`, a digest of
-  the flute outline and a non-convex sweep. That is issue 896's work. The
-  four kinds here are parametric and need none of it. Issue 896 stays open
-  for corner rounding, back chamfer and slitting saws.
-- *A new `SimOp` field for the undercut.* `SimOp` has about 90 literal
-  construction sites. The undercut rides `Planned::undercut` in the app
-  and `Stock::simulate_undercut` in the sim crate instead.
-- *New neck fields on `Tool`.* Not needed (see above); the file format and
-  every tool dialog stay as they are.
-- *Multiple depth levels.* One level per operation: the head cuts the
-  whole undercut height when the cutter matches the slot. A taller
-  undercut takes a second operation with another Bottom Z.
-- *Round far ends.* The far end links offsets with a straight lateral
-  feed. The cutter centre never leaves the band within the shift of the
-  centre line, so the undercut is never wider than asked; a blind end is
-  left square by up to the shift.
-- *Picked geometry.* The centre line is typed (as the Slot's is). A pick
-  law for undercut faces is follow-up work.
-- *Cutting the neck with the column engine.* It would be correct only
-  where the neck slot is narrower than the neck (a collision the law
-  already refuses), so it adds nothing.
-
-**Literature search (review follow-up, 2026-11-19)**
-
-The original implementation preceded this search. This follow-up checks its
-choices against published material; it does not change that history. The
-search used the web search tool because no Perplexity tool was available.
-Queries covered T-slot preparation and side entry, dovetail and lollipop
-contact geometry, distance-field CSG, and tri-dexel machining simulation.
-Only public Autodesk behaviour documentation, a machining handbook, and
-published research support the findings below. No camlib implementation,
-HSMWorks source, binary, output trace, or bundled asset was inspected.
-
-Checked sources and the choices they support:
-
-1. Walter, [Technical Compendium — Milling, 2024, section D2,
-   page D 140, “Strategies for preparing a T-slot”](https://cdn.walter-tools.com/files/sitecollectiondocuments/downloads/global/manuals/en-gb/technical-compendium-milling-2024-en.pdf).
-   The indexed section describes a prepared opening that extends below
-   the shoulder to leave the cutter shank clear. This supports checking
-   the neck against the opening as well as the head against the slot.
-   Our additional allowance for each radial pass follows from the neck's
-   lateral displacement. The handbook gives machining preparation
-   advice, not a proof of collision freedom for an arbitrary entry.
-2. Autodesk, [Sketch profile selection](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/ENU/Fusion-CAM/files/MFG-GEOMETRY-SELECTION-SKETCH-PROFILE.htm),
-   and [Is it possible to create a keyway undercut with a Slot operation
-   in Fusion?](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Is-it-possible-to-create-a-keyway-undercut-with-a-Slot-operation-in-Fusion.html)
-   (2025-11-04). The first describes tapered walls cut with a dovetail
-   cutter and clearance at both path ends. The second describes a gouge
-   with an ordinary slot path and returning to the entry position.

-   construction is more restrictive: descend at one outside station,
-   enter and leave laterally at depth, then retract at that station.

-   from tip-based spacing. The second identifies the ball diameter as a
-   limit on access to tight corners. These support using the actual
-   profile instead of treating the cutter as a point at its tip.

-   disc and a narrowing frustum reach their largest radius at the bottom;
-   a sphere reaches it at the equator. These coordinates are our
-   derivation, not formulas copied from the documentation.

-   Fields: A General Representation of Shape for Computer Graphics](https://www.merl.com/publications/docs/TR2000-15.pdf),

-   Boolean carving of object and tool fields. Section 3 discusses
-   sampling resolution and reconstruction error. This supports removing
-   swept head and neck solids from a volumetric field that can retain a
-   roof. It does not require a one-height stock model or establish our
-   sweep search's accuracy.

-   sign convention for min/max CSG and warns that a combined field need
-   not remain a Euclidean distance field. It also describes aliasing and
-   resolution limits. Our inference is to sweep each convex head/neck

-   convex search to the complete non-convex cutter. This paper supports
-   the set representation, not the convex-search convergence claim.

-   Volumetric Models to Polyhedral Surface Models for Product
-   Prototyping](https://www.cad-journal.net/files/vol_5/CAD_5%286%29_2008_932-941.pdf),
-   Computer-Aided Design & Applications 5(6), 2008, pp. 932–941,
-   DOI 10.3722/cadaps.2008.932-941, sections 1 and 6. The paper describes

-## #1445 - Fine boring (G76): the shift is in the cycle choice and in the chain; only a post that declares the cycle writes it
-
-**What was decided.**
-
-1. Fine boring is a new cycle choice on the drilling operation,
-   `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }`, and a new CL cycle
-   kind, `CycleKind::FineBore`. The shift is a required part of the choice.
-   There is no default shift.
-2. The chain makes the shift. A hole's group is: feed in, a lateral rapid
-   at the bottom (the shift), a rapid out at the shifted XY to R, a rapid
-   back onto the hole axis at R. The `Cycle` and `CycleRec` records get no
-   new field.
-3. The post engine reads the shift from the chain and gives it to the
-   script as `ShiftX` / `ShiftY`. It refuses the cycle by name for a script
-   that does not declare `fineBoring = true`, and for a chain with no shift
-   move.
-4. Only the Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes
-   `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole, and never `Q`.
-   Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
-5. A machine file can state `spindle.orientation: true|false`.
-   `false` refuses a fine bore by name, with any post. An unstated value
-   is "not limited", as for `spindle.rigid_tapping`.
-6. The shift must be smaller than `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`. The
-   generator refuses a larger shift by name. The command refuses a zero
-   shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift not smaller than a
-   hole radius.
-7. The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped
-   bar. Law (d) and the solid law do not read the cutting-edge zone on
-   these moves. The solid law still reads the shank and the holder at the
-   shifted position.
-8. The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, not to
-   the flute length. The hole is there already, as for a bore and a ream.
-
-**Why.**
-
-- #1479 asks for an explicit shift: "A guessed default could drag the tip
-  across the finished bore, so no default is posted." A choice that cannot
-  exist without its shift makes that a type rule. The integer micrometres
-  keep `CycleChoice` `Copy` and `Eq`, and they are the lattice the chain
-  uses.
-- A shift held in the chain cannot disagree with the posted shift. The
-  WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and
-  the cycle centre together, so the posted `I` and `J` are correct in each
-  frame with no new code. A new field on `Cycle` or `CycleRec` would need a
-  transform in each of those places, and it would change about 50 struct
-  literals in tests.
-- The chain as plain moves is not safe on a control: the shift would move
-  a turning tool into the finished wall. So the refusal is in the engine,
-  for each post that does not declare the cycle. A future post is refused
-  until it declares the flag. The author of a post does not have to
-  remember the cycle.
-- The Haas `G76` takes `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y (Haas Mill
-  Operator's Manual, G76 Fine Boring Canned Cycle). The `Q` form takes its
-  direction from Setting 27, which a program cannot state. So the post
-  never writes `Q`.
-- The verifier models a tool as the cylinder that its turning edge sweeps.
-  That cylinder, shifted by `s`, overlaps the bore wall by `s`, and the
-  verifier refused each fine bore. With the spindle stopped, the bar
-  reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches
-  `tool radius - s`. Both are inside the cylinder that the feed in cut
-  while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over that
-  same cylinder. The shank and the holder are above the edge zone and are
-  not inside that cylinder, so they keep their reading.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-
-- A `shift` field on `Cycle` and `CycleRec`, with a `SHIFT` word in the
-  `.cl` and `.cnc` texts. Dropped for the reasons above.
-- A separate `fine_bore_shift` field on `OpParams::Drill`. It permits a
-  fine bore with no shift, and it changes about 70 test files that build a
-  drill operation.
-- `G76` with `Q` on the Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan posts. The direction of
-  `Q` is a control parameter (Fanuc parameter No. 5101). A program cannot
-  state it, so the posted shift could go into the wall. These posts refuse.
-- Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, Sinumerik `CYCLE86`, Mach4 `G76`. Each needs
-  words that the operation does not have (a spindle angle, a disengaging
-  direction code), or a word layout that this work did not read from the
-  maker's manual. These posts refuse. The follow-up issue names them.
-- An expanded chain with `M19`. The orientation word and its angle are
-  different on each machine. #1479 asks for a refusal.
-- A refusal when `spindle.orientation` is not stated. No shipped machine
-  file states it, so each machine would refuse. The unstated-limit law
-  already governs `rigid_tapping`; this capability uses the same law. The
-  post is the second door.

-  a holder that the shift moves into a clamp or a wall. Only the edge zone
-  is acquitted.
-
-**What it trusts.** The tip points against the shift at the oriented stop.

-bar diameter is the tool's shank diameter. The shift is along the X and Y
-of the hole list (the model frame); the post writes it in the frame of the

-
-**Not done here.**

-## #1480 - Back bore (G89) carries the dwell and feeds out at the plunge feed
-
-**What was decided.** The drill generator (`camcraft_motion::drilling::drill`)

-  G-code reference). The cycle exists for its dwell, and the user could not
-  get one.

-  dwell) has one F word. The post takes that F from the first cutting move
-  of the hole's chain, which is the plunge. So the control always fed out at
-  the plunge feed. The chain said the cutting feed. The verifier, the
-  simulation time and the `.cl` dump then disagreed with the machine. The
-  Ream cycle (G85, #1445) already uses the one-feed chain; Back bore now
-  uses the same law.
-- Each post reads the dwell in seconds from the stream and writes its own
-  P unit, or refuses by name. Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan, Haas and Sinumerik write
-  whole milliseconds; grblHAL, Tormach, LinuxCNC and Mach4 write seconds;
-  Heidenhain writes an explicit dwell block. The lathe posts and the posts
-  with no canned cycle refuse the Back bore.
-  `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`, `haas_dwell_cycles.rs`,
-  `mach4_post.rs`, `heidenhain_cycles.rs` and `sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs` pin
-  these words (#2350, #2360).
-- Sinumerik G89 now writes `P0` for zero dwell. This clears a previous
-  positive dwell instead of leaving its modal P active. The Siemens
-  [ISO dialects Function Manual, 07/2021](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf),
-  table 6-1, printed page 95, gives the G89 dwell unit in milliseconds.
-  Section 6.3.1 describes modal cycle parameters. The tests
-  `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds` and
-  `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p` pin the unit and its reset.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-- Keep the feed out at the cutting feed, and make each post write a second F
-  word. A canned cycle has no second F word. A post would have to expand the
-  cycle into G1 moves, which changes every Back bore program.
-- A separate "retract feed" parameter for bore cycles. This is a new
-  parameter and a new command field. It is not necessary for this issue.
-- A new G89 golden for each post in this PR. Direct assertions pin each
-  P word. The Sinumerik tests also pin the transition from positive dwell
-  to zero.
-
-**Cost to change later.** Small. The feed out is one line in
-`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`, pinned by
-`back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`. A Back bore program with no
-dwell keeps the same F. Its Sinumerik G89 block now includes `P0` to clear
-a previous dwell. The `.cl` chain of a Back bore changes its feed-out feed.
-On the Heidenhain post,
-which writes the Back bore as an explicit chain, the retract line now has
-the plunge feed.

-## #1591 - 3D Adaptive: Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level
-
-**What was decided**
-
-- `OpParams::Pocket3D` has a `method` field (`AdaptiveMethod`: Spiral or
-  Trochoidal). It is read only under the Adaptive strategy. The default
-  is Spiral.
-- Under Trochoidal, each level of the plain ladder is planned by the 2D
-  lane planner (`plan_all_lanes`, `plan_cleanup`) on the cutter-centre
-  area that the ladder already has. The new module
-  `machining2d::adaptive_troch_level` plans, posts and checks one level.
-  `machining3d::troch` holds the run state and the new entry point
-  `pocket3d_trochoidal`.
-- A level that the method refuses is cut by the Spiral plan. A note says
-  why and names the Z of the level. The level is built on a copy of the
-  path, so a refusal posts nothing of the trochoidal attempt.
-- The material top is proved, not assumed. A trochoidal level can leave
-  stock, so a later bore or plunge starts above the deepest trochoidal
-  level whose cleared area holds its disc. If no level holds it, the
-  bore starts above the stock top. A proved bore starts on the proved
-  plane, as the ladder's own descents do. Thus the helices of two levels
-  share no depth and cannot cross.
-- In a trochoidal run, each level enters as a first level does. This
-  includes a fallback (Spiral) level below a fallback level. No level
-  reads the plane above as cleared. The cost is a longer descent in air
-  on a run where many levels fall back.
-- Each posted level is checked against its level area and against the
-  crossing law. The crossing check reads the level's own moves and all
-  moves before it.
-- The rest pass, the offset shells and the rotary wrap keep the plan
-  that they had. Their existing notes say so.
-- The method is passed as an argument of the internal `ladder`, not as a
-  field of `Pocket3DParams`.
-- The project file writes `method` as a word for each 3D Pocket, as 2D
-  Adaptive does. A file without the word reads as `spiral`. No format
-  version was added.
-- The stamp gets one more byte only under Adaptive with Trochoidal.
-- Under Trochoidal the footprint does not use the Adaptive air band
-  (#1950). The loops are not planned from the air.
-
-**Why**
-
-- The level area of the ladder is the level law: footprint less the
-  part above the plane, eroded by the tool radius and the stock to
-  leave. Loops inside it are inside the level area and beside the
-  model. The posted level is checked again, move by move.
-- The 3D descents (`descent.rs`) read the plane above as the material
-  top. That is true after a Spiral or ring level. It is not true after
-  a trochoidal level that left stock. A rapid to that plane could hit
-  stock. Thus a trochoidal run proves the top or uses the stock top.
-- After a trochoidal level the tool is at the end of that level, not on
-  the plane of an older fallback level. A keep-down level link would
-  feed from there through stock that the loops left. The "Do not touch"
-  keep-out of #2149 also reads the plane above as the top of the band
-  that a descent crosses. With no plane above, the keep-out covers the
-  full height, which a bore from the stock top needs.
-- A level area of a 3D part is often narrow near a wall. A refusal of
-  the whole operation for one such level makes the method hard to use.
-  The issue permits a fallback by name.
-- A `method` field in `Pocket3DParams` changes 74 struct literals in 28
-  test files. An argument of `ladder` changes 7 internal call sites.
-- A Spiral operation has the same stamp as before. Existing 3D
-  Adaptive operations do not go Stale.
-- The MCP params patch refuses a key that does not come back from the

-## #1696 follow-up - a full-window shot from the real renderer (GUI test
-finding)
-
-**What was decided.** The maintainer's second GUI test said the shot must
-be the whole application window, not just the 3D model area. The door now
-asks the shell for a window picture the way egui intends: the report path
-pushes `egui::ViewportCommand::Screenshot` with a private token. The frame
-loop (`shell_window/capture.rs`) sees the command in the root viewport's
-output and, in the same frame after the normal egui pass, draws the same
-tessellated shapes a second time into a private texture
-(`RENDER_ATTACHMENT | COPY_SRC`, the surface config's size and format)
-in its own render pass. It then copies the texture to a mapped buffer and
-answers egui with `egui::Event::Screenshot`, which the door reads: on a
-matching token it copies the picture to the clipboard with
-`Context::copy_image` and says so in the status line. SolidCraft
-(tangency-labs/solidcraft) was read as mechanism reference only -
-their public API use, no code, no look (their brand licence).

-**Why.** egui's own screenshot responder lives in eframe; our shell
-drives winit and `egui_wgpu::Renderer` itself, so nobody else answers the
-command. A second pass in the same frame is the only way to catch the
-window as the user just saw it: the report dialog the user pressed is
-still up, and its shapes are already tessellated. Reading back the
-surface texture itself is not possible: wgpu does not make the swap-chain

-without trying: its readback rejects the `Bgra8UnormSrgb` surface format

-that was exactly the complaint.

-  allocates nothing for a zero-sized payload, so every `UserData::new(())`
-  shares one pointer and all tokens compare equal. The shot token is a
-  `OnceLock` `UserData` over a non-zero string; the unit test
-  `the_shot_token_matches_only_itself` pins both halves of the law.
-- Delivery: egui 0.36.2 has no `Context::send_event`, so the map callback

-  `raw_input.events` before `ctx.run_ui`. The loop keeps
-  `request_redraw` alive while a readback is in flight, so the answer
-  lands without user input.
-- Format: the swizzle table maps RGBA (0,1,2,3) and BGRA (2,1,0,3);

-## #1862 - A DXF profile on the stock of a setup, and the virtual model reference
-
-The maintainer's words (issue 1862, 2026-11-15): "A DXF should be possible to
-"place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a
-model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just
-make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly.
-The Adding DXF Profile, should thus live on "Stock page" and have a "virtual"
-model reference, just so the operations pages gets happy about a model being
-loaded.."
-
-### What a profile is in the ECS
-
-- **A `Sketch` component on a named entity** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`),
-  beside `Name` and `Location`. It holds `setup: Option<String>` (the
-  declared-vs-effective law of `Operation::setup`) and `data:
-  Arc<SketchData>`. The entity never has `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is
-  false for it, so the part readers (`model::model_entities`) and each 3D
-  solid tool do not see it.
-- **`SketchData` is in `camcraft-geometry`** (`sketch_data`), not in `app`:
-  it works only on domain values. It holds the primitives in millimetres, the
-  layer names, the source units (the file's `$INSUNITS` and the unit applied),
-  the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. Its
-  fields are private and the two constructors make the chains, so the stored
-  chains are always the chains of the stored primitives.
-- **The `Location` of a profile is relative to the stock**, as the scope
-  change says: the frame is the top face of the stock of the setup, at the
-  stock origin, turned with the stock (`sketch::face_frame`). The stock origin
-  is the origin of the stock entity (for a box and a cylinder: the centre in
-  XY). The top is the box height, the cylinder height, or the highest facet Z
-  of a stock made from a model. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face
-  normal only. Because the placement is relative, a moved or resized stock
-  carries the profile, and nothing must follow it by a second command. The
-  stock is setup furniture, so a setup's part alignment does not move the
-  profile.
-- **Deleting the entity frees the drawing.** The component is a Rust-owned
-  type; the last `Arc` holder drops the data
-  (`deleting_the_entity_frees_its_drawing`).
-
-### The commands
-
-- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** reads, checks and chains
-  the file at construction. `setup` is the new argument (`None`: the active
-  setup). A setup without a stock is refused ("make a stock first"). A file
-  with no unit and no unit from the caller is the typed
-  `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing`; it has the drawing extents, so the UI of
-  issue 1863 can show them in each unit before it asks. A unit from the caller
-  wins over the unit of the file (the argument is an override).
-- **`MoveSketch` moves a profile; `MoveModel` refuses one by name.** The issue
-  body said `MoveModel`. That was written before the scope change. `MoveModel`
-  writes a world placement and carries the stock; a profile has a face
-  placement (X, Y, angle) and rides the stock. Two verbs on one object would
-  split the undo story (the "pages own their verbs" law of `MoveModel`), so
-  the profile has its own command and the placement cannot leave the face.
-  Dropped: a `MoveModel` that accepts a profile and silently drops Z and tilt.
-- **A name from the file stem is made unique** (`plate`, `plate (2)`), so one
-  drawing can be placed more than one time on a sheet. A stated name that is
-  in use is refused.
-- **`DeleteSetup` refuses a setup with a placed profile** (as it refuses one
-  with operations). Dropped: deleting the profiles with the setup, which loses
-  work without a word.
-- The Z of the drawing (`Document::elevation`) is not used: the profile lies
-  on the stock face.
-
-### What the virtual model reference is
-
-- **It is derived, not stored**: `sketch_model::of(world, setup)` is `Some`
-  when the setup has one or more placed profiles and the document has no part
-  (a model that is not a fixture). No component and no file key holds it, so
-  it cannot disagree with the document. Dropped: a tag component or a
-  placeholder model entity. A placeholder entity must be kept in step by each
-  command that adds or removes a model or a profile, and a facet-less "model"
-  in `model_entities` is the zero-triangle mesh that the issue forbids.
-- **It has no facets.** It names profiles only.

-

-### What was decided and why
-
-- **Extend `FeatureSel` with `SketchChain(ChainId)` and `SketchLayer(String)` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).**
-  `FeatureSel` drops `Copy` and derives `Clone` so `SketchLayer` can carry the layer name directly across UI state, commands, MCP IDs (`sketch_chain:<hex>` / `sketch_layer:<name>`), and `PROJECT_VERSION = 74` (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs`).

-  Each override keys on `(entity, chain: ChainId)` with optional `side: Option<ChainSide>` and `reverse: bool` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`). `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from `73` to `74` (main took v73 for #2055) so older builds refuse files carrying sketch picks or per-chain overrides instead of silently dropping them, while v73 files load unchanged.

-- **Natural nesting when uniform, ordered per-chain generation when overridden (`crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch.rs`).**
-  Whole sketches (`SrcRef::Entity`) and layer/chain picks with unmodified `Auto` sides and uniform `climb` check `can_group_natural` and cut as one nested `Region` (holes Inside, outers Outside). When per-chain `side` or `reverse` overrides diverge, closed chains generate in hole-before-outer order so inner bores clear while the part still holds them. Preserved closed polylines and sampled arcs keep true CL `ArcMove` geometry so `posting` emits `G2`/`G3`.
-- **Explicit open-chain safety (`validate_plan` in `crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch.rs`).**
-  Open DXF chains cut along the centerline only. Operation-level `Side::Inside`/`Side::Outside`, any per-chain `ChainSide` override on an open chain, and control/wear compensation (`G41`/`G42`) refuse by name, naming the sketch chain; `reverse: true` remains allowed to flip centerline direction.

-- **Meshless generation and verification (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/material.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`).**
-  `sketch_model::generation_problem` admits `OpParams::Contour`, and `material::named_material` returns the placed sketch stock-top height with empty facets for `Sketch` entities (`part_solid = false`). Unresolved `TopOfModel`/`BottomOfModel` heights still refuse via `sketch_model::NO_SOLID_HEIGHT`. Stock removal (`stock_sim::simulate_document`), crossing, stock-rapid, and fixture collision checks run against setup stock and fixtures without requiring a 3D solid mesh.

-## #1868 - Slot and Trochoidal Slot on DXF sketch chains
-
-**What was decided**
-
-- A Slot and a Trochoidal Slot read one picked chain of a DXF profile.
-  They keep their two points and their width (`a`, `b`, `width`). The
-  project file does not change, and no version bump is necessary.
-- The pick seeds the numbers in the pick's own command
-  (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick
-  and the seed. This is the law that #1504 made for model picks.
-  - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`.
-  - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The
-    typed `width` stays.
-- Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain, as the world
-  is at that time. A slot that left its outline, or whose ends are not the
-  ends of its centerline, is refused by name. A moved or re-imported
-  profile cannot cut in the old position.
-- A closed chain is a slot outline only when the fitted straight slot
-  covers 99.5 % or more of the area of the chain. A rectangle, a circle, an
-  L or a keyhole is refused by name.
-- A selection with more than one chain is refused by name. The whole
-  profile as the source is refused by name.
-- The refusal of a Slot that is narrower than the tool now gives the two
-  numbers.
-
-**Why**
-
-- The room law of `machining2d::SlotBound` (#1504) is reviewed and pinned.
-  A sketch outline is a face room, and the existing fit and confine laws
-  apply without a second algorithm. A centerline is one new room kind
-  (`Room::Line`) with a small law of its own.
-- Seeded numbers stay visible and editable on the operation page. The
-  generator, the machine area, the WCS rotation and the verification read
-  `a`, `b` and `width` in many places. A second source of slot geometry in
-  the job would need a change in each of them, in safety code.
-- The stock simulation and the verification use the setup stock
-  (`part_solid = false`), as #1864 made for the 2D Contour.
-- The area test refuses an outline that only contains a slot. The model
-  face law of #1504 accepts a rectangular floor as a room, because a floor
-  face is the room of a slot. A drawn outline is the slot itself, so the
-  rule is stricter.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- Bent and arc centerlines (an open chain of lines and arcs). The plain
-  Slot generator cuts a straight channel only. The Trochoidal Slot
-  generator takes a point chain, but its machine area, its fit law and its
-  parameters have two points. A curved channel needs a new parameter form
-  and a new machine area. Such a chain is refused by name. This needs an
-  issue of its own.
-- Closed chains as centerlines (a circular groove). A closed chain is read
-  as an outline only. One chain cannot be the two things without a new
-  parameter, and a wrong guess cuts in the wrong place.
-- More than one chain in one operation (a layer of slots). The operation
-  holds one `a`, `b` and `width`. Each slot is one operation for now.
-- New `SrcRef` or `OpParams` fields for the sketch. The existing
-  `SrcRef::Selection` with `FeatureSel::SketchChain` / `SketchLayer` of
-  #1864 holds all that is necessary.
-- An analytic read of the outline (two lines and two half circles from the
-  chain segments). The area test accepts the same outlines, and it also
-  accepts an outline whose arcs a CAD system wrote as short lines.
-
-**Cost to change later**
-
-- Curved centerlines add a parameter form. That is a project file change
-  with a version bump.
-- The 99.5 % limit is one constant (`OUTLINE_COVER` in
-  `operation/slot_sketch.rs`).
-- The messages of a judged sketch outline say "the picked face" (the text
-  of the face room). A separate room name is a small change in
-  `slot_room.rs`, which is near the 400-line limit.
-
-## Review corrections
-
-**What was decided**
-
-- Group natural contour chains only within one profile entity. Parent
-  checks use both the entity and the chain ID.
-- Key sketch highlights by the placed world pose. Keep `None` in the key
-  when the sketch has no stock.
-
-**Why**
-
-- Independent profiles can nest in world space while both resolve to an
-  outside cut. A combined region can turn the inner profile into a hole
-  and reverse its cut side. Separate generation keeps the resolved sides.
-- A chain ID belongs to one profile. An equal ID in another profile is
-  not its parent.
-- A profile rides its stock. The highlight position changes when the
-  stock moves or its height changes. Without stock, the profile has no
-  placement and draws no highlight.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- Grouping chains from separate profiles by chain ID alone. This loses
-  entity identity and can change the resolved cut sides.
-- Using a sketch's local `Location` as the highlight key. That value
-  does not change when the stock moves, changes height, or is removed.

-## #1873 - Core cadmpeg runner, version check and temp-dir sandbox
-
-### 1. No `cadmpeg formats --json` probe; the exit status of `check` and `convert` is the capability test
-
-**What was decided.** The runner does not call `cadmpeg formats`. It runs
-`--version`, then `check --json <input>`, then
-`convert <input> -o <out> --to step --reject-lossy=export`. A build that
-cannot read the input format or cannot write STEP fails one of these with
-a nonzero exit status, and the import is refused with cadmpeg's own last
-error line.
-
-**Why.** The issue asks for a `cadmpeg formats --json` probe. cadmpeg
-0.6.12 has no such option: `formats` takes no arguments and prints a text
-table (the first worker on this issue found this; the CLI definition at
-tag commit `9d7592c64` confirms it). cadmpeg's own source says that the
-table is for a terminal reader and is not for a caller to parse. The
-probe was only an early diagnostic. Safety does not depend on it: `check`
-and `convert` give the verdict, and the STEP importer's guards run on the
-result.
-
-**Dropped.**
-- Parsing the text table of `cadmpeg formats`. Its layout is not a
-  contract, so a new cadmpeg could silently break the import.
-- A JSON schema of our own that only the stub answers. It proves nothing
-  about cadmpeg.
-- Waiting for an upstream JSON contract (the first worker's
-  recommendation). It blocks #1875, #1876 and #1877 on a third party. The
-  probe can be added later without a change to the pipeline.
-
-**Cost to change.** One more step in `cadmpeg::to_step` before `check`.
-
-### 2. The check verdict is the exit status, and the JSON report is read as a second guard
-
-**What was decided.** A nonzero exit status of `check` refuses. With exit
-status 0, the runner still reads the JSON on standard output. It refuses
-when a `findings` list at any depth has an entry with severity `error` or
-`blocking`, and when the output is not JSON.
-
-**Why.** cadmpeg's README states that `check` exits 1 on `error` and
-`blocking` findings, so the exit status is the documented contract. The
-report layout is versioned by cadmpeg and can move; the scan by key name
-does not depend on the path of the list. A report that the runner cannot
-read cannot clear a part (Prime Directive).
-
-**Dropped.** A typed model of the report. Its schema is not ours and no
-real report was available in this environment (cadmpeg is not installed).
-
-### 3. The child writes to files in the private folder, not to pipes
-
-**What was decided.** Standard output and standard error of the child go
-to two files in the private folder. One loop looks at the child, the
-clock and the file sizes every 15 ms. A child that passes the time limit,
-prints more than 16 MiB, or grows the STEP file past the size limit is
-stopped. The folder is removed by a `Drop` guard.
-
-**Why.** With pipes, a reader thread blocks for as long as any process
-holds the pipe open, also after the child is stopped. With files there is
-no reader thread, and "bounded buffers" is a size that the loop reads. No
-new crate is needed.
-
-**Dropped.** Stopping the whole process group of the child. That needs
-`libc` (`kill` on a negative pid) or `unsafe`; the issue forbids new
-dependencies. Only the direct child is stopped. cadmpeg is one process.
-
-### 4. Refusals use `CommandError::Needs`; an unusable binary uses `CommandError::Invalid`
-
-**What was decided.** A missing program, an old version, a wrong stated
-path, a failed `check`, a failed `convert`, a time-out and an oversized
-output are `Needs`: plain text that the user can act on. A program whose
-`--version` text states no version is `Invalid`. An unqualified native
-extension keeps `CommandError::UnsupportedType` with the extension, as
-IGES had.
-
-**Why.** `Needs` shows the text with no "invalid parameters:" prefix
-(#1105). `UnsupportedType` keeps the existing IGES tests and UI status
-text unchanged.
-
-### 5. The qualified table is empty, and the stated path is used alone
-
-**What was decided.** `import::native::QUALIFIED` is empty, so no import
-reaches the runner in a shipped build until #1875 adds a format. All
-extensions that cadmpeg lists as inputs (`.prt` included) are refused by
-name. When `cadmpeg_path` is set and is not a program file, the import
-refuses; it does not fall back to `PATH`.
-
-**Why.** The issue says to keep the table empty. A silent fallback would
-run a different program than the one the user named.
-
-**Also.** `ImportModel::within` reads the preferences file for the
-stated path (`Settings::from_prefs`) because the command constructor has
-no settings argument; #1876 owns the UI field. Until then the UI keeps a
-hand-written `cadmpegPath` when it saves the preferences.
-
-**Not done here.** The `wasm32` refusal text and the UI wording belong to
-#1876. In this PR the runner module is compiled only off `wasm32`, and a
-qualified extension on `wasm32` or in `ImportModel::from_bytes` refuses by
-name.

-## #1888 - Deburr: picked edges, excluded edges, minimum edge angle, hole filter
-
-**What was decided**
-
-1. **Picked chains narrow the ride; they do not bound a region.** A Deburr
-   whose source is a selection with edge chains breaks only the exposed
-   edges on those chains. `OpParams::Deburr` stays in the `selection_drives_region`
-   list of mesh-driven kinds. The picks are read by a new module,
-   `operation/deburr_picks.rs`, the way Multi-Axis Contour reads its drive
-   chains. A source that is a whole model, the stock, or a selection with
-   no edge chain keeps the automatic detection.
-2. **A pick selects among exposed edges only.** A picked chain that lies on
-   a concave or flat meeting is not ridden. The path has a note for it. If
-   no pick names an exposed edge, generation refuses by name.
-3. **A pick is not filtered.** The minimum edge angle and the hole filter
-   judge the automatic edge set only. An excluded chain is removed in both
-   modes.
-4. **A face, patch or vertex pick in the source keeps its old meaning.**
-   It names the model that the ride reads and does not narrow the ride
-   (`setup_align_deburr.rs` pins this reading, #2284). `exclude_edges`
-   holds chains only; `is_sane` refuses a face, a patch or a vertex there.
-   An excluded chain that is no longer in the model is refused by name.
-5. **New operations get 40 degrees; old files get 0.** The seed sets
-   `min_edge_angle_deg` to 40.0. A project file without the key reads 0.0
-   (every crease), which is the ride the file stored. Each new key is absent
-   from the file at its rest value, so an old file saves unchanged. The
-   operation stamp digests a filter only off its rest value. An automatic
-   or face-only operation keeps its legacy stamp and cached path. A
-   chain-selected operation gets a selection-law version in its stamp and
-   must regenerate once. The previous generator ignored those chains.
-6. **The hole filter matches the bore's own cylinder.** A recognized hole
-   (`drilling::recognize`, `recognize_cross`) whose diameter is in the range
-   removes each exposed edge with both ends on its cylinder, within 0.05 mm,
-   inside the wall's span. The seed range is 0 to 10 mm, with the filter off.
-7. **The picked and the excluded chains share the job's `drive_chains`
-   slot.** The source's chains come first; the pick count of the source
-   says where the list splits. The WCS yaw then turns both lists with the
-   facets, with no new slot.
-8. **The UI moves picks into the exclusion list.** The Deburr page has the
-   button "Exclude the picked edges". It adds the edge picks of the
-   Selection block to the draft's `exclude_edges`. Apply writes them with
-   the other parameters, as one `EditOperationParams` command.
-
-9. **Exclusion models are cache dependencies.** The stamp includes each
-   referenced model's geometry and placement in the setup frame. A missing
-   model makes the stamp unresolved and the cached operation stale.
-
-**Why**
-
-- The issue text says to remove Deburr from the `!selection_drives_region`
-  guard. That guard sends the picks to `selection_region`, which makes a 2D

-## #1945 - AI provider HTTP clients, keychain keys and offline-only mode
-
-**What was decided.** A new `camcraft_app::ai` module holds the provider
-transport: `endpoint` (URL parse, loopback test, the offline and https laws),
-`presets` (Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini over https;
-Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio and llama-server on loopback), `wire` (the
-request path and body per provider, echoing tool-call envelopes so reasoning
-items and Gemini thought signatures survive), `probe` (Ollama `/api/show`
-capabilities), `secret` (an opaque `ApiKey`, environment first, then the
-keychain), and, native only, `http` (the client) and `keychain`. The AI Chat
-dock uses it through `transport_http::HttpTransport`; the browser build keeps
-the offline-only default transport and links no socket or keychain code.
-`prefs.json` gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on), and the dock's
-"Offline only" switch is saved there.
-
-**New third-party crates (need the maintainer's decision).** `reqwest 0.12`
-(default features off, `rustls-tls-webpki-roots`) provides HTTP(S).
-`tokio 1` uses `rt`, `time`, `net` and `macros` for a current-thread runtime
-per request. `keyring 4.2` provides macOS Keychain, Windows Credential
-Manager and Secret Service over zbus. `url 2.5` was already in the lock and
-is now a direct dependency. These dependencies still need the maintainer's
-decision. This change adds no dependency between CamCraft crates.
-
-**Why these.** The first version used blocking `ureq 2.12`. Review #2122
-found that its active request could not be cancelled. A silent server could
-therefore block chat shutdown for the full request timeout. The client now
-selects between the async request and a cancellation check every 20 ms.
-Cancellation drops the request and its runtime, which closes the active
-connection. The Ollama capability probe uses the same cancellation path.
-A detached blocking request was rejected because it would remain active
-after cancellation. rustls avoids system TLS dependencies. keyring 4's
-Linux store uses Rust over zbus, so the release runners need no `libdbus`
-build package.
-
-**Provider errors remove secrets.** JSON and plain-text provider errors
-remove the supplied API key before the message is truncated. This also
-removes a key that crosses the text limit.
-
-**Offline-only is enforced in the client, twice.** `endpoint::admit` refuses
-a non-loopback host before anything resolves; the client's resolver then
-refuses any resolved address that is not loopback (a hosts-file `localhost`
-pointing elsewhere). No redirect is followed: a local server could otherwise
-bounce a call to a remote host. `no_proxy` disables environment proxies,
-so a loopback request cannot use a remote proxy. Plain `http://` off the machine is refused
-whether or not a key is sent - cloud providers are https only.
-
-**Unsloth Studio and llama-server bases.** The issue names
-`http://127.0.0.1:8888` for Unsloth Studio; the base is
-`http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, the OpenAI-compatible mount every other local
-runtime here uses. llama-server's documented default port is 8080; its label
-says to start it with `--jinja` for tool calls.
-
-**A model without tools refuses, it does not silently degrade.** When an
-Ollama model in the native-tools preset lists no `tools` capability, the
-step is refused by name, pointing at the Prompt-JSON and Q&A presets. Falling
-back inside the transport would send a request without the prompt-JSON
-context (the transport has no project snapshot) and the reply would not parse.
-
-**Considered and dropped.** Blocking `ureq` (no active request cancellation);
-`native-tls`
-(OpenSSL headers on Linux); keyring's `dbus-secret-service` store (vendored
-libdbus C build); storing keys in `prefs.json` encrypted (the issue forbids
-any key there); an MCP tool to set a key (an agent should never handle a
-user's secret).
-
-**Cost to change later.** Low for presets and wire shapes (data and pure
-functions with loopback tests); swapping the HTTP crate touches only
-`ai/http.rs`.

-## #1951 - A batch suite step starts its test executable from the build's cargo JSON artifacts
-
-**What was decided.**
-
-- Each batch prebuild (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`) has the flag
-  `--message-format=json-render-diagnostics`. The executor keeps the JSON messages of the build and makes
-  one `cargo metadata --no-deps` call. From the two it records the test executables of the crate
-  (`xtask/src/artifacts.rs`).
-- A suite step of that crate (`--lib`, `--bins` or `--test <name>`) then starts the recorded executable
-  and does not start cargo (`xtask/src/direct.rs`). The step name, the step number, the log file name and
-  the plan are the same. `--dry-run` prints the same cargo commands.
-- The executable starts as `cargo test` starts it: in the package directory, with the libtest args after
-  `--`, and with the variables that cargo sets (`CARGO`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH`, the
-  `CARGO_PKG_*` set, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<bin>`, `OUT_DIR`, the `rustc-env` pairs of the build script and the
-  dynamic library path). The list was read from a test process under cargo 1.100.
-- The gate writes cargo's `Running <target> (<path>)` line into the step log before the output of the
-  executable. `read_log`, the notes and `--failed` read the log as before.
-- A step stays a cargo step when one of these is true: its package has no recorded build in this run
-  (`--only` or `--failed` selected the step without its build step); its target has no executable in the
-  list; it is a `--doc` step; its args are not exactly the known form. The printed command shows which
-  way a step ran.
-- The executable path comes only from the JSON list. The gate never searches `target/` for one.
-- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` makes each step a cargo step again. It is for a comparison run, and for a
-  platform where a direct run does not behave as `cargo test` does. This PR ran on macOS only.
-
-**Why.**
-
-- Each suite step started cargo to run one binary that was built already. The issue gives about 0.5 s for
-  one start on Windows, and the batch plan has several hundred suite steps.
-- This PR is stacked on #2788. That PR builds each crate alone, so the executables of the build are the
-  same ones that `cargo test -p <crate>` runs. With one build for all the crates the features are
-  unified, and the executables are different ones.
-- cargo 1.100 puts a test executable in `target/debug/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out/`, not in
-  `target/debug/deps/`. A path that the gate computes itself is wrong on one of the two layouts. The JSON
-  list is correct on the two.
-- When the gate runs under `cargo xtask`, its own process has the `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `CARGO_PKG_*`
-  values of `xtask`. A direct run must set the values of the tested package. If not, a test that reads
-  one of them at run time gets the wrong value.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**

-- The release tier. Its debug build is one build for all the crates (feature unification). Its steps
-  stay cargo steps. A change to builds for each crate changes the plan of the cut gate; that is not in

-## #2012 - Depth ladder: the remainder ladder stays the default, equal steps is an opt-in parameter
-
-**What was decided**
-
-1. The default ladder does not change. It steps down by the full stepdown
-   from Top Z, and the last step keeps the remainder. `top 20, bottom 2,
-   stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
-2. Equal steps is an operation parameter, `equal_steps`, off by default. It
-   is a field of the operation's `links.approach` object
-   (`camcraft_motion::approach::Approach`). On, the ladder cuts the same
-   number of levels, and each step is the span divided by that count. The
-   same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
-3. The mode is one function, `machining2d::equal_stepdown(top, bottom,
-   stepdown)`. It gives the stepdown that the unchanged level law
-   (`cut_levels_under`) then walks. `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom,
-   stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. The
-   generators call it in place of `cut_levels_under`.
-4. With stock over Top Z (#2004) the level at Top Z stays, and the steps
-   under it are equal.
-5. The stepdown stays the largest step. Code that reads `stepdown` as a
-   bound (the 3-D shell's floor under a plane, the contour's first entry
-   height) is not changed: with equal steps it reads a bound that is a
-   little larger than the real step, which is the safe side.
-6. The parameter is on the operations that have a `links` object: 2D
-   Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Circular, Slot, Bore, 3D
-   Pocket and the rotary / multi-axis roughing that run the 3-D ladder.
-7. The app's pocket region law (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the
-   same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`, so the region is built at
-   the planes that the generator cuts.
-
-**Why**
-
-- The default must not move posted G-code. Each golden file and each saved
-  project keeps its programmed depths.
-- The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter, not
-  for a silent change of the law.
-- The `links.approach` object is already saved field by field (absent means
-  default), already rides `EditOperationParams` for undo, and is already
-  what the MCP `edit` tools parse. A new field there needs no file version
-  step and no new command.
-- One function for the mode keeps one level law. No second ladder can drift
-  from the first.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- Equal steps as the new default. Dropped: it changes the posted depths of
-  each multi-level operation in each saved project.
-- A second level function with its own loop (levels computed as `top - i *
-  span / n`). Dropped: two loops with two float behaviours for one law. The
-  mode as an adjusted stepdown reuses the tested loop and its refusals.
-- A field on each parameter struct of the motion crate. Dropped: Face,
-  Trace and Trochoidal Slot have about 30 struct literals in tests and
-  callers, and the operations have no `links` object to save the choice in.
-- Replacing `stepdown` in each generator's parameters before the run, so
-  that each reader sees the equal step. Dropped: Bore and the Circular
-  vault have one span for each hole or ring, so only the level law knows
-  the span.
-- A row beside each Stepdown field on the Passes tabs. Dropped for now: the
-  field is saved in `links.approach`, and the one editor of that object is
-  the Lead in / Lead out tab. The row is in its Linking group.
-
-**Not done here (follow-up #2832)**
-
-- Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They keep
-  the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them.
-- Turning has its own infeed laws (`turning/*`). They are not part of this
-  decision.
-
-**Cost to change later**
-
-- To make equal steps the default: change `Approach::DEFAULT.equal_steps`,
-  write the field when it is `false`, and regenerate each golden of a
-  multi-level operation. Old files without the key would then read as equal
-  steps, so that change also needs a file version step.
-- To remove the parameter: delete the field and its DTO key. Files that
-  have the key still load (unknown keys of `approach` are ignored only if
-  the DTO stays tolerant; check before the removal).

-## #2016 - A tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
-
-**Decided.** A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a
-reference: the entry's exact name, the gauge length and the projection
-(`camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef`, on `ToolBody::library`).
-The project file and the `.camtools` file write it as the tool key
-`holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true`
-for an assumed holder, #828) and write no `body`. One function turns a
-reference into a shape, `tool_body::build_library`; the command
-(`SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool`), the project loader and the tool
-library reader all call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the
-simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before.
-
-**The document keeps the resolved body beside the reference.** The
-`ToolBody` component still holds the outline, facets and bands. They
-are derived data: nothing but `build_library` writes them for a library
-holder, and no file stores them. The laws therefore read exactly the
-steel they read before, with no second resolution path. Resolving on
-every `judged` call was dropped: it would add a refusal path to every
-law and gain nothing, since both lengths are stored in full.
-
-**Both lengths are stated in the reference**, also when the caller left
-them out (the entry's gauge length, the tool's flute plus shank length).
-A later edit of the tool's lengths therefore does not move the holder;
-`tool_body::fits` refuses at use when the holder no longer fits, as it
-did for the drawn copy.
-
-**Same shape, pinned.** For every library entry, at its default and at
-other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, the envelope, the
-band stack, the stamp term and the facets of the referenced holder
-equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored
-(`holder_reference::every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`).
-The stamp term is unchanged, so no operation goes stale.
-
-**Migration: an older file is not rewritten.** A file without `holder`
-loads as it did. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a drawn
-(custom) profile with the same outline; a `holder_d`/`holder_len`
-cylinder stays the tool's own numbers. Neither is turned into a
-reference: the copy may have been edited, and matching an outline back
-to an entry is a guess. The user picks the entry again to get a
-reference.
-
-**Version step.** Project files write v70 (`PROJECT_VERSION = 70`),
-after v68 (#2441) and v69 (#1517) on `main`, and `.camtools` files write
-version 4 (`HOLDER_REF_VERSION = 4`, after `CUTTING_STEPS_VERSION = 3`)
-when a tool names a library holder (keeping earlier minimum versions
-when no tool names one). `v0.22.0` reads project v62 and `.camtools` 2,
-and pre-#2016 builds read up to project v69 and `.camtools` 3; both
-refuse v70 and version 4 instead of dropping `holder` and judging the
-tool's smaller holder cylinder.
-
-**Refusals.** A reference to a name the library does not hold refuses
-the file by tool name, and so does a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon", which
-names no bore), lengths the entry cannot be drawn at, a holder that
-reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, and a tool
-that states both `holder` and `body`. No other holder is put in its
-place (#808). The shank fit is checked when the holder is set, not on
-load: a file the app saved must open, and a drawn copy was not checked
-on load either.
-
-**A change of the library's own numbers now reaches old projects.**
-A reference is drawn from the build's tables. If an entry is corrected,
-every tool that names it follows. That is the point of a reference; a
-copy kept the old numbers.
-
-**Editing.** The outline of the referenced holder applied unchanged
-(Apply profile, MCP `points`) keeps the reference. One edited point
-makes it a custom drawn profile, in one undo step.
-
-**Tool library import.** The import's "same tool" test still compares
-the shape (the body as a save wrote it before). A drawn copy and a
-reference with the same outline are therefore the same tool and are
-skipped, not added a second time as "Name (2)".
-
-**The holder fields.** With a referenced holder the tool settings show
-the holder diameter and length the laws read (the cylinder that
-encloses the entry) as text, not as two fields. The tool record's own
-`holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten: they are what the tool
-goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move
-the tool's stamp. An assumed (machine default) holder keeps the two
-fields, because #828 floors it at them.
-
-**MCP.** `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference;
-`get_job` and the reply show it as `holder.library`. A `holder`
-reference inside `add_tool`'s `definition` is refused by name (the
-definition's body was never read there; dropping a reference would land
-the machine's default holder in its place). `edit_tool` refuses a
-`holder` patch like `body`.
-
-**Dropped.** Removing `holder_d`/`holder_len` from the tool record (every
-law and every file reads them; the stand-in cylinder of a bare tool
-stays). A reference field on `Tool` itself (the body component already
-carries undo, the file key and the delete hook). User-defined library
-entries (the reference names built-in entries only; a user library is
-separate work).
-
-**Breaking.** A project or tool library saved with a library holder is
-not readable by v0.22.0 and older (project v70, `.camtools` version 4).
-`ToolBody` has a new public field.
-
-**Cost to change.** Small. The reference type, `build_library`, the
-`holder` key (`project/tool_body_wire.rs`) and its readers.

-## #2055 - "Do not touch" protected faces and edges on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket
-
-### What was decided
-- **Operations covered in this first slice**: `OpType::Offset2D` (`2D Offset`) and `OpType::Pocket3D` (`3D Pocket`) obey `"Do not touch"` across all strategies (`Waterline`, `Zigzag`, `Auto`, `OffsetRings`, `Adaptive`, `shell`, `rest_rough`, `feed_opt`), all `Entry3D` modes, all `Links` modes (including `KeepDown` level checks and elevated rapid traverses), and tilted 3+2 planes (`Offset2D { tilt: Some(...) }`). Unsupported operation kinds refuse non-default `"Do not touch"` by name across commands, UI, MCP, and generation so nothing is silently ignored.
-- **Storage on `AreaControls` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs`, `avoid.rs`)**: Added `pub do_not_touch: DoNotTouch` inside `AreaControls` (with `has_boundary_edits()` separating 2D region boundary clipping from `"Do not touch"` and preserving exact legacy behavior/stamps when `DoNotTouch` is default), avoiding edits to 185 `Operation` literals while automatically propagating through undo/redo, paste, stale tracking, and UI drafts.
-- **Independent 3D verification & generator keep-outs (`crates/sim/src/verify/avoid.rs`, `avoid_links.rs`, `avoid_poly.rs`)**: Added `Warning::AvoidHit { at, item, part, short_mm }` (`Copy`, `blocks_post() == true`). Per-Z-interval keep-out regions (`AVOID_PAD = 0.02 mm`) dilate Z-clipped triangles and 3D edges by each tool stack band (`Flute`, `Shank`, `Holder`) plus `clearance + max(stock_to_leave, 0)`, while `avoid::hits_named` (`AVOID_VERIFY_TOL = 1e-4 mm`) sweeps every move independently across all stack bands and midpose chords.
-- **Per-level planners & rapid link elevation**: Extracted `pocket_avoid` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`) and `avoid`-aware `pocket3d_avoid` (`ladder.rs`, `shell.rs`, `entry.rs`), checking `prev_center` on `KeepDown` links and elevating obstructed horizontal rapid moves via `elevate_rapid_links`. Rest-roughing skips safely with a note if only protected columns remain unmachined after a clean roughing ladder.
-- **Commands, MCP, UI, live post gate, and project format v64**:
-  - `SetOperationDoNotTouch`, `EditOperationParams`, `SetOperationGeometry`, `ChangeOperationKind`, and `EditOperationLinks` validate picks (rejecting vertices) and refuse overlap between protected items and the machining selection or `Include` boundaries by name.
-  - Added `get_operation_do_not_touch` / `set_operation_do_not_touch`, `"do_not_touch"` on `get_operation_geometry`, `"Do not touch"` controls under `Geometry` -> `Boundary` -> `Boundaries`, and persistent viewport highlighting (`avoid_viz.rs`) while an operation is selected.
-  - Bumped `PROJECT_VERSION` `63 -> 64` (stacked on `#2077`) so older builds refuse `.camproj` files that carry `"do_not_touch"` protection rather than silently dropping it.
-
-### Why
-- Separating `has_boundary_edits()` from `is_default()` on `AreaControls` lets `Offset2D` and `Pocket3D` use `"Do not touch"` without altering 2D boundary containment/extension semantics or existing stamps/goldens.
-- Using one independent 3D full-stack verifier (`sim::verify::avoid`) across generation (`verify_avoid`) and posting (`live_avoid_problems` + `blocks_post`) prevents any generator quirk, rapid hop, or post-generation part move from ever emitting unsafe G-code.
-- Extending `PROJECT_VERSION` prevents pre-v64 readers from silently discarding protection and cutting protected geometry.
-
-### Considered and dropped
-- Storing `do_not_touch` directly on `OpParams` or `Operation` instead of `AreaControls`: rejected because it touches hundreds of struct literals and duplicates copy/paste/draft plumbing that `AreaControls` already handles.
-- Rolling out across all 2D/3D/multi-axis/turning operations in one PR: rejected in favor of a tight, end-to-end verified first slice (`2D Offset` and `3D Pocket`) that avoids stacking conflicts with open PRs `#1817`, `#1822`, `#2037`, and `#2093`.
-
-### Cost to change later
-- Extending `"Do not touch"` to additional operation kinds (`Pocket`, `Adaptive2D`, `Contour`, `Finish3D`, etc.) is additive: add the `OpType` variant to `do_not_touch_applies` and pass `avoid_spec` to that generator arm; `verify_avoid`, `route_links`, UI, commands, MCP, and v64 project format already work unchanged.
-
-### Merge refresh against main v66
-
-Main now writes project v66 for the trunnion schema (#1962), following
-cutting rows (v64) and the tilt basis (v65). The protected-pick format must
-therefore write v67. Reusing v64 or v66 would let an existing reader accept
-the file and silently discard `do_not_touch`. All earlier migrations and
-refusals remain. The project test pins a version beyond v66, protection
-round trips, future-version refusal, and blocked posting after a moved
-protected item. Reusing main's version was rejected because it would weaken
-that protection. Main's carried-stock replan and previous-stock mask are
-kept together with the protected-item planners.
-
-### Merge refresh against main v70 and review fixes (#2149)
-
-Main advanced to `PROJECT_VERSION` 70 (v68 for Drill `break_through_from`, #2441; v69 for Pocket Adaptive retirement, #1517; v70 for library holder reference, #2016), added `cut_levels_under` (#2004), `pocket3d_open_prev` (#1950), `Field::new` in `crossing_hop_tests`, and `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` Frame cost rules (#2238) + pick-highlight caching (#2201). On the merged branch:
-- `PROJECT_VERSION` steps `70 -> 71` for `"do_not_touch"`, keeping v68, v69, and v70 migrations and refusals intact.
-- `pocket3d_avoid`, `pocket3d_open_avoid`, and `pocket_avoid` keep `cut_levels_under` and `air_stock` while preserving `avoid` keep-outs, `Field::new` is restored alongside `Field::new_with_avoid`, and `Warning::AvoidHit` coexists with `Warning::DrillUndersize`.
