-## #2158 - Deterministic true-shape nesting in camcraft-geometry
-
-**Decided.** Integrate the held CamCraft nesting kernel from
-`origin/issue/2158-nesting-kernel` into the current geometry crate. Keep the
-existing `nesting.rs` entry point and its public raster module. Add no ECS,
-world access, or crate dependencies. The algorithm follows Bennell and
-Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell (OR 2006,
-EJOR 2007); no third-party nesting implementation supplied code.
-
-- Compute NFPs from convex decomposition and Minkowski sums on the existing
-  `geo2d::SCALE` integer grid. Preserve zero-width seams swallowed by polygon
-  unions so exact-fit cavities remain candidates. Compute rectangular IFPs
-  from bounds and closed-hole IFPs from the container complement's NFP.
-  Keep triangulation and its slab fallback local to nesting.
-- Place parts with deterministic bottom-left-fill. Sort by decreasing outer
-  area, then stable part id, then instance index. Try permitted rotations
-  and mirrors, deduplicate equivalent footprints, and cache local NFPs.
-  Outer-area ordering places a hollow frame before parts that can use its
-  holes even when the frame's net material area is smaller.
-- Apply separate-cut inflation by cut side: `cut_width + part_gap / 2`
-  outside, `cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2` on line, and `part_gap / 2`
-  inside. Buffer open chains with `Region::sweep`. Offer an explicit router
-  single-slot mode and refuse it when `part_gap < cut_width`.
-- Reduce the sheet by `edge_margin` with `Region::offset_sharp`, then keep
-  each cut footprint inside that usable sheet. The footprint already
-  includes outer cutter clearance, avoiding double-counting at the edge.
-- Search usable holes before allocating a new sheet. Treat placed hole
-  occupants as filled outer obstacles within their parent's hole. Expose
-  their own holes separately and report the immediate containing part.
-  Require empty intersection and outside-difference regions during exact
-  verification; a small positive overlap is not accepted as a tolerance.
-- Check requested-quantity addition and refuse totals above 10,000
-  instances by name. This bounds placement work and report allocation.
-  Report counts, net-area utilization, used bounds, waste regions, and
-  named unplaced quantities without producing toolpaths or G-code.
-
-**Why.** Reusing the held clean-room work preserves its existing geometry
-coverage while adapting only the entry point and refusal checks to current
-main. Convex decomposition makes concavities and swept-chain polygons use
-the same geometry operations. Explicit seams retain exact fits, while the
-final region checks enforce clearance independently of candidate generation.
-
-**Dropped.** Orbital NFP sliding needs more state around collinear edges and

-larger hollow host. Raster-only placement cannot establish exact vector
-clearance. Changing `geo2d::Region::triangles()` would broaden this issue;

-functions. Another search heuristic or a configurable quantity budget can
-replace those policies without changing the geometry primitives. Raising
-the quantity cap requires performance and memory measurements. Changing the
-public input or report structs requires updating downstream nesting users.

-## #2194 - Playback keyframes share the cut bricks that no move changed
-
-**What was decided.** The three cut layers of `SdfField` (`cuts`, `cut_ups`,
-`cut_downs`) hold each brick in an `Arc` (`CutLayer` in
-`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`). A clone of the field copies the keys
-and the pointers only. A write goes through `layer_brick_mut`, which uses
-`Arc::make_mut`: it copies a brick first when a clone still holds it. The
-keyframe store counts a keyframe by `KeyCost::key_bytes_after`: the bricks
-that the keyframe before it does not share, and the map entries of the three
-layers.
-
-**A visit is not a write.** `claim_record` and `up_record` read the cell
-first and take the writable brick only when the value changes. Before, they
-took the writable slot first. With shared bricks that copied each brick that
-a move reached, also when no cell changed. On the staged 24 mm face the
-read-first order holds 9.9 MB for 28 keyframes; without it 16.4 MB; whole
-copies cost 45.3 MB. The values that the cut writes are the same, bit for
-bit: an absent brick reads NaN, and NaN always took the write.
-
-**Why.** A keyframe was a whole copy of the cut layers (#2181). Two keyframes
-one stride apart differ only in the bricks that the moves between them
-touched. Sharing the other bricks lets the same 512 MiB budget hold more
-keyframes, so the stride stays short on a large program. Copy-on-write keeps
-each keyframe an exact prefix of the program: no write can reach a brick that
-a keyframe holds. The map entries are counted because a store of fully shared
-keyframes would otherwise cost "0 bytes" and escape the budget.
-
-**The count can read high, never low.** The test for "shared" is pointer
-identity with the keyframe before. Each brick allocation is counted at the
-first keyframe that holds it. A live seek that restores an old keyframe and
-cuts again makes equal bricks in new allocations; those count again, which is
-what the memory holds. After a thinning the store sums again from the keys
-that stay.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-- A delta chain (each keyframe stores only its changed bricks, a restore
-  walks back to key 0). Dropped: a restore would cost a walk over all
-  keyframes, and a thinning would need a merge of deltas. Shared pointers give
-  the same memory with a restore that is one map clone.
-- An exact count with a set of all brick pointers in the store. Dropped: it
-  needs the store to know the brick type, and the pairwise count is already
-  never low.
-- `Arc` on the whole layer map (as the mesh layer has). Dropped: the first
-  write after a keyframe would copy every brick again.
-- Share the mesh-layer bricks one by one too. Dropped: that map is already
-  shared whole and is written only while the field is built.
-
-**Cost.** Each cell write does the `Arc::make_mut` uniqueness check (two
-atomic operations, no lock). The swept-distance evaluation of the cell
-dominates it. `CostLedger` (the cut region, the full-brick ledger, the dirty
-set) is still copied whole by each keyframe and is not counted, as before.
-
-**Cost to change later.** `CutLayer` and `layer_brick_mut` are the only
-places that know the brick is shared. A different store (a pool, an arena)
-replaces those two and `cut_bytes_after`.

-  dropped at the load, and a load that fails puts the default layout back.

-## #2343 - Rotary Parallel leaves the end face of a held end
-
-Sources: chuck and tailstock practice from machine-tool handbooks; our own
-raster, link and stock code. No Fusion or HSMWorks material was consulted.
-
-- **Decided: Rotary Parallel reads the setup stock and leaves the end face of
-  a held end.** Where the stock goes on past an end of the model along the
-  fitted axis by more than one tool diameter (plus the tolerance), that end is
-  a held end: the bar goes on into a chuck or onto a centre. At a held end the
-  centre of the ball does not go past the end plane of the model. The
-  operation adds a note that names the end and the distance. A free end, where
-  the stock ends with the model, is cut as before. **Why:** the end-face pass
-  at a held end is a slot one tool diameter wide from the skin of the bar to
-  its axis. That parts the bar. The post blocked it only for a tool with a
-  short flute. The stock already says where the bar goes on, so the generator
-  can know this without a new setting.
-
-- **Decided: the limit is one tool diameter.** Stock that goes on by one tool
-  diameter or less is a facing allowance. The end-face pass removes all of it
-  and leaves no disc on the bar. That case does not change. More than one
-  diameter leaves a disc that the pass cuts off, so it is a held end.
-
-- **Decided: the centre of the ball stops on the end plane.** The turned
-  surface is then finished to its end, and the verification reports no rest
-  there. Half of the ball goes past the plane. There it cuts no deeper than
-  the surface that it rides on, so the bar past the model keeps the radius of
-  the model's end or more. **Dropped:** the centre one radius inside the
-  plane, so that the ball never crosses it. I built this first. It left a
-  strip one tool radius wide with the fillet of the ball, and the example got
-  a scallop warning of 0.749 mm against a gate of 0.520 mm. The model was not
-  finished to its tolerance, and the user had no way to finish it.
-
-- **Decided: a sloped entry does not start past a held end.** With the
-  sloped-entry law (a tool that is not centre-cutting), a ramp whose top is
-  past the plane is not used. That infeed stays a radial plunge, and the
-  centre-cutting guard judges it as before.
-
-- **Decided: a model with no length between two held ends is refused by
-  name.** No pass fits there.
-
-- **Dropped: a new setting** (an axial window with two stations, or "leave
-  the end faces"). It needs a parameter, a project-file version, a UI field
-  and an MCP field. It is a `feat` and waits for the maintainer. With it, a
-  user could also keep the pass off a free end face, or cut a held one.
-
-- **Dropped: a refusal at each held end.** It makes the job impossible on a
-  held bar, which is the usual way to hold rotary work.
-
-- **Dropped: a warning only.** The program would still part the bar.
-
-- **Not changed: Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset.** They read their heights
-  as stations and already have an axial window.
-
-- **Limit.** The generator knows only the stock that the setup states. If the
-  stock ends where the model ends but the real bar goes on (the kit job of
-  #2342), CamCraft reads air there and cuts the end face as before. The guide
-  pages say this. A model with a domed or coned held end is still cut on that
-  dome or cone, up to the end plane.
-
-- **The #1904 example.** The example project and program are generated again.
-  The program has no feed move past X-1.25. A 1/2 in flute now posts, because
-  the shank refusal came from the cut that is gone. The guide page drops its
-  "air cut only" limit and keeps the air cut as the first run.
-
-- **Cost to change later.** A setting can replace the stock reading: `held`
-  then returns the window from the two stations. `clip` and the callers stay.

-## #2373 - Isolate the live theme between parallel unit tests
-
-**Decided:** Keep the production live theme in its process-wide
-`OnceLock<RwLock<Tokens>>`. Under `cfg(test)`, use a thread-local
-`Cell<Tokens>` initialized to `Tokens::DARK`. Extract the storage helper to
-`theme/live.rs` so the theme table stays near the 400-line limit.

-that selects Light must not change the ground colors another test uses
-when scanning overlay colors. Color-vision selection already belongs to

-that shared input lets the existing tests run in parallel without changing
-the application's runtime theme behavior.
-
-**Considered and dropped:** Adding `snapshot_guard()` around every theme
-reader and writer would serialize the tests and rely on every future
-consumer remembering the lock. Using thread-local storage in production
-would change runtime behavior across threads. Running all tests serially
-would hide the interference instead of isolating their state.
-
-**Limits and later cost:** This test-only isolation does not prove that
-production theme access is safe across a sequence of operations on several
-threads. A future unit test that renders on another thread must explicitly
-install its tokens there. Changing the storage policy later is a small,
-local helper change; callers keep the same `current` and `set_current`
-interface.

-
-**What was decided:**
-- Add `CornerRelief` (`kind`, `tbone_direction`, and per-corner `overrides` matched by XY) to `OpParams::Pocket`, `OpParams::Adaptive2D`, and `OpParams::Offset2D`, with empty/off defaults.

-  the parse; a mesh handed in and a browser pick record none. The record

-  that keeps the fidelity keeps it), `DeleteEntity` (delete and undo) and
-  `ImportFixture`'s update. Generated meshes (vise, plate, accessory,

-- **Project v72** (`project/source_dto.rs`): an optional `source` on a
-  model row. Absent is not linked, so a v71 file steps up unchanged. A
-  source on a row that is not a model, an empty path, a digest that is not
-  64 lowercase hex digits, or an unknown key in it is a corrupt file. An
-  older CamCraft refuses a v72 file by name (`unsupported project version
-  72`), as for every version step: it would otherwise save a linked model
-  back unlinked without a word.

-  window about once a second (`INTERVAL`), and the frame timer comes back
-  for it while a model is linked. A file is read again only when its size
-  or modification time moved. When its SHA-256 is not the model's, the

-  is called. The landing is the existing re-import: one `UpdateModel`, one
-  undo step, the operations go Stale. Nothing regenerates or posts.
-- **Undo stays.** The check remembers the digest it last imported for each
-  model and does not import the same bytes again. An undo of the import
-  thus stays until the file changes once more.
-- **A missing or unreadable file** leaves the model as it is. The status
-  line says it one time, by name; the check says nothing more until the
-  file is readable again.

-  step). The MCP tool `set_model_link` links (to a path, recording its

-## #2474 - WCS flip: a flipped Z stays refused, with the exact reason
-
-**What was decided.** A flipped Z does not post. The refusal stays at the two
-doors (the verification gate, `app::setup_wcs_flip`, and the post engine,
-`post::wcs_flip`). It now names the exact reason instead of a general one.
-The two doors read the reason from one constant (`post::wcs_flip::Z_REASON`).
-The issue permits this result: "or the refusal names the exact reason and the
-decision is recorded".
-
-**The exact reason: the tool-length word.** A flipped axis reads the same
-physical point with the other sign. For X and Y the mirror is complete in the
-program: signs, G2/G3 and G41/G42 follow from geometry. For Z, one word does
-not follow from geometry: the tool-length word.
-
-- The tool is on the physical "up" side of its tip. On a control that reads Z
-  reversed, "up" is the control's -Z.
-- A register that holds a preset length (a positive number from a presetter)
-  then needs the subtracting word, G44.
-- A register that holds a length touched off on that control already has the
-  control's sign. It needs the adding word, G43.
-- The project states only "Z is flipped". It does not state how the tool
-  lengths were measured. The two cases need opposite words.
-- The wrong word moves the tool by twice its length, toward the work in one of
-  the two cases. A note in the program cannot make that safe (Prime Directive).
-
-**The second reason: canned cycles.** A drilling cycle states an R plane and a
-hole bottom. A mirrored Z puts the R plane on the far side of the hole bottom.
-The public standards (RS-274 / NIST RS274NGC, ISO 6983) define the cycles with
-the R plane above the bottom, and some controls refuse the other order. The
-post engine names this only for a section that has a canned cycle.
-
-**The open questions of the issue.**
-
-- "Is a flipped Z a real machine setup?" Yes, it can be: a machine whose Z+
-  moves toward the work (some routers), or a fixture frame that points down.
-  The first is a machine property (`"direction": -1`, #374), and that door
-  refuses Z for the same reason. The decision does not depend on the answer:
-  the two cases have the same unknown tool-length word.
-- "Which dialects can state a negative tool-length direction?" Fanuc and Haas
-  have G44. LinuxCNC has G43 only. Heidenhain and Siemens do not use the word
-  pair. This is from general machining knowledge and was not checked against
-  each manual. A carry by G44 alone cannot cover each built-in mill post.
-
-**What was dropped.**
-
-- *Mirror Z and keep G43, with a program note.* Wrong by two tool lengths for
-  preset registers.
-- *Mirror Z and swap G43 to G44 (the geometric rule, as G41/G42).* Wrong by two
-  tool lengths for touched-off registers, and not available in each dialect.
-- *Expand the canned cycles into plain moves for a flipped Z.* It solves the
-  second reason only. It has no use while the first reason refuses.
-
-**What a carry needs (the maintainer decides).** One new statement from the
-user: how the tool lengths of the flipped setup are measured (preset, or
-touched off on the control). With it, the post can select the word, or refuse
-a dialect that cannot state it. That is a new parameter with its command, MCP
-tool, project-file field and one equivalence test for each dialect
-(`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, a reader with Z flipped that models the
-tool-length word). The setup sheet, the travel check and the viewport envelope
-need no change while Z is refused.
-
-**Cost to change later.** Low. The refusal is one branch in each door and one
-shared constant. The X and Y mirror (`invert::translate_rules`) already
-negates Z coordinates when asked; the cycle branch and the tool-length word
-are the open parts.

-## #2476 - Carry a WCS XY flip with a Z rotation
-
-**What was decided**
-
-- Keep the existing pass order: WCS flip, WCS rotation, then any
-  machine-axis inversion. Bake mirrors the existing setup/table
-  coordinates. Control rotates those mirrored coordinates using the yaw
-  expressed in the mirrored frame. The existing passes carry arc
-  centres, starts and stock bounds with the moves.
-- Reverse the controller's G68 / ROT angle when exactly one of X and Y
-  is flipped. Keep its sign when both are flipped. Keep that composition
-  in the shared Rust passes so every rotation-capable dialect receives
-  the same transformed stream.
-- Allow a Z-yaw WCS through the app's flip validation. Keep named refusals
-  for other rotations and nonfinite placements: "only a finite Z rotation
-  is supported with flipped axes". Keep refusals for flipped Z, probing
-  and the operation types the mirror does not carry. Keep the existing Control
-  capability checks and its refusal with inverted machine axes. A non-XY
-  arc in a rotated WCS remains refused by the rotation pass.
-- Keep the existing travel and setup-sheet behavior. Travel judges the
-  mirrored table-frame path after the controller rotation, independently
-  of the output mode. The sheet states the setup's original yaw and its
-  flipped axes.
-
-**Why**
-
-A reflection and a rotation do not commute. Write the XY mirror as `F`,
-its determinant as `d`, and the original yaw as `a`. The flip pass states
-`a1 = d * a`. The rotation pass then produces
-`R(-a1) F (p - O) = F R(-a) (p - O)`. The controller applies `R(a1)`
-in its mirrored frame, so the physical path is
-`F R(a1) R(-a1) F (p - O) = p - O`. One flipped axis has `d = -1`;
-flipping both XY axes has `d = 1` and preserves the angle sign. The
-existing mirror also carries the arc-direction and cutter-compensation
-side changes.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- Reorder rotation before reflection. A mutation that restored the old
-  pass order still passed the Control pin: conjugating the yaw in the
-  flip pass makes that order equivalent. The reorder adds no behavior,
-  so it was dropped.
-- Keep refusing every combined flip and yaw. The existing rotation and
-  mirror passes can carry the supported milling cases with the
-  conjugated yaw.
-- Add separate mirror-angle rules to each post script. A shared stream
-  transform gives each dialect the same geometry and avoids duplicated
-  rules.
-- Add dependencies or another placement representation. The existing
-  WCS flags, yaw parameter and record transforms express the operation.
-
-**Cost to change later**
-
-The angle parity and composed physical path are part of the posting contract.
-Adding another controller rotation convention must preserve the traced
-physical path. Extending flipped Z, probing, tilted work or inverted
-machine axes in Control mode still needs its own proof and named
-capability handling; this change does not remove those refusals.

-## #2575 - A new worktree seeds its target/ from another checkout
-
-**Decided.** Before its first step, `cargo xtask gate` copies the dependency units
-(`target/debug/{build,deps,.fingerprint}`) of the checkout with the most units into a new
-worktree. Cargo then finds `solidcore`, `flecs` and the build-script crates Fresh. The copy:
-
-- skips each package without a `source` in `cargo metadata` (workspace members and path
-  dependencies): their sources are in the checkout, and an older copy can read as Fresh
-  with other code;
-- replaces a unit that is there already (`cargo xtask` builds its own dependencies first),
-  else its newer time makes each copied unit above it dirty;
-- keeps the modification times, copies outputs before fingerprints, and renames each unit
-  into place, so a stopped copy only causes a compile;
-- takes cargo's locks of the two directories without a wait, and passes over a checkout
-  where a build runs;
-- writes `target/debug/.camcraft-seeded` once. `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` turns it off.
-
-**Why.** sccache 0.19 hashes the `OUT_DIR` value of each env dependency, the cwd and the
-raw arguments of a Rust compile. `OUT_DIR` names the worktree, so each build-script crate
-misses, and each crate above it misses too. `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` applies only to C and C++.
-Cargo's fingerprints do not name the worktree, so a copied unit is reused. Measured on an
-18-core Mac (APFS clones, sccache warm): the first app test took 107 s without the seed
-and 42 s with it (9 s seed, 24 s step). 231 units compiled without it, 14 with it.
-
-**Dropped.**
-- A `--remap-path-prefix` in RUSTFLAGS: sccache hashes the raw argument, which names the
-  worktree, so all keys would change in each worktree.
-- A shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or `build-dir`: AGENTS.md forbids the first, and the two lock
-  out parallel gates of other worktrees.
-- A change to sccache (normalize `OUT_DIR`): outside this repository.
-- Copy only the units that the gate needs: cargo has no stable unit graph to name them.
-
-**Cost to change.** One module (`xtask/src/seed.rs`) and one call in `gate`. Removing it
-returns the gate to the sccache-only behaviour.

-  part tree. It reads as an empty tree, not as a refusal. The 3-axis parent
-  chain is pinned on `vmc.mch`, which is the same machine in the file form.

-  the part id and the key: a part with no `id`, an `id` stated two times, a

-**What was decided.** The STEP importer now measures the mesh it keeps. For
-each curved elementary face (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus) it measures the
-chord height of every facet edge inside the face against the face's own
-surface. An edge that stands more than twice the pass tolerance off the
-surface is split at the surface, round by round, until none does
-(`geometry/import/step_fit.rs`). An edge on the face's boundary is never
-split, so the shell stays closed. A chord height that cannot be refined
-away (the facet budget, the round cap) becomes the chord error that the
-import reports. The model then carries reduced fidelity (#864) and the
-gate refuses to verify against it.
-
-**Why.** The issue says that tilted operations are not judged for gouges.
-That is not the cause. A tilted operation is judged at generation, in the
-plane's frame, by the keep law (`contain_into`, #1603). The test
-`a_tilted_slot_into_a_meshed_bar_is_refused` shows this on unchanged code.
-The cause is the reported part. It is a D50 bar with two cross holes, from
-a STEP file. The kernel (truck) triangulates a trimmed face in its
-parameter plane. A cylinder's parameter grid has two rows, and the two are
-on the boundary, so no grid point is inside the face. With a hole in the
-wall, each rim edge was joined to the hole's rim a quarter turn away. The
-facets ran through the solid, up to 25 mm inside the true cylinder. The
-importer reported the tolerance that it had asked for, not the error of
-the mesh that it got. Every gouge law (generation, the program sim, the
-upright operations too) then judged the cut against a part that was too
-small. The slot at A0 was convicted only because the mesh is correct next
-to the hole at the top.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-

-  second option of the issue. It refuses every 3+2 and rotary program,
-  although the generator-time laws judge them (`posting_sim.rs`, pinned by
-  `post_not_judged.rs`). It also does not fix the report: the upright sim
-  reads the same wrong mesh. The maintainer can still decide on an
-  override design; this PR does not change that policy.
-- *Only report the measured error.* Smaller, but each bar or tube with a
-  cross hole is then refused as "imported too coarsely", and a larger
-  facet budget does not help. Refinement gives a correct mesh.
-- *Stretch the parameter plane of elementary faces* (as #1602 does for
-  B-spline faces), or give the triangulation interior rows. This gives the
-  better mesh with fewer facets. It changes the triangulation of every
-  cylinder face of every model, and its effect on the goldens is not
-  known. It is follow-up work.
-- *Measure B-spline, NURBS and swept faces too.* Their grid is #1602's
-  and one evaluation is more expensive. Not measured here; stated in the
-  module header.

-the kernel's mesh was wrong: the reported bar goes from 1 084 facets to

-face that the kernel meshes correctly is not changed. The slack of two
-tolerances keeps a mesh that meets the kernel's own test as it is; a lower
-slack would change more meshes.

-findings on mills through the existing detection command.

-The solid core between their floors must remain outside both hole depths.
-A span check alone does not identify the entry side. Floor evidence gives

-the floor as part of this bore, even when subdivision adds interior vertices.

-## #2612 - Nesting raster 1: conservative bit-packed rasteriser
-
-**Decided (unattended, issue-worker-high):**
-
-- **Place.** `camcraft_geometry::nesting::raster` (`crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster.rs`
-  and `raster/scan.rs`). No new crate, no new crate edge, no new external
-  dependency.
-- **Integer decisions.** Region vertices are quantized with the `geo2d`
-  Clipper-bridge rule (`geo2d::quantize`, 1 unit = 1 um). All cell tests
-  are exact `i128` arithmetic with checked multiply and add. No float takes
-  part in a cell decision.
-- **One algorithm, two outputs.** Two integer passes: (1) "touched" - each
-  cell whose closed square touches a closed boundary edge (row slabs, with
-  the x extent of the edge in the slab rounded outward: floor of the
-  minimum, ceiling of the maximum); (2) "centre inside" - even-odd parity of
-  a +x ray at each cell centre, with the half-open edge rule of
-  `geo2d::Loop::contains_xy`, in doubled coordinates so that the centre is
-  an integer. Over = touched OR centre inside. Free = centre inside AND NOT
-  touched. Why this is safe: a closed square that meets the region but no
-  boundary edge is fully in the interior, so its centre is inside; a square
-  that no edge touches and whose centre is inside is fully in the interior.
-- **Rounding direction.** Always outward for "touched": a value on a cell
-  line touches the two cells; the x extent in a slab is widened to whole
-  units. This can mark one extra cell, never one fewer.
-- **Cell packing.** Rows of `u32` words, `ceil(width / 32)` words for each
-  row. Cell `i` is bit `i % 32` (least significant bit first) of word
-  `i / 32`. Padding bits are always zero. `u32` matches a WGSL storage
-  buffer word for the later GPU slice.
-- **Grid origin.** `RasterGrid::covering` snaps the origin down to a multiple
-  of the cell size (the global lattice), so that part and sheet rasters at
-  the same cell size share one lattice and a placement moves in whole cells
-  (research comment 2 on #2525, rule 3). `RasterGrid::new` takes any origin.
-- **Cell-size default.** `DEFAULT_CELL_UNITS` = 1 mm (the coarse level of
-  the coarse-to-fine search of #2525).
-- **Cell limit.** `MAX_CELLS` = 2^24 (4096 x 4096, one fine tile of #2525)
-  and `MAX_SIDE` = 2^16 on a side. A 3000 x 1500 mm sheet at 1 mm (4.5e6
-  cells) fits. A larger grid is `RasterError::GridTooLarge`.
-- **A part that does not fit is refused.** `rasterize_over` returns
-  `RasterError::RegionExceedsGrid` when the region bounds are not in the
-  closed grid extent: a clipped part raster is no longer an
-  over-approximation. `rasterize_free` clips freely: a cell outside the
-  region is never free, which is the safe side.
-- **Empty region.** `RasterGrid::covering` refuses it (`EmptyRegion`); the
-  two rasterize functions return an all-zero raster for it.
-
-**Dropped:**
-
-- Float scanline with an epsilon: not exact, and an epsilon can lose a
-  touched cell.
-- Rasterize the Minkowski-inflated part here: the spacing inflation belongs
-  to the placer slice; this slice takes the region that it is given.
-- `u64` words: `u32` is the native word of a WGSL storage buffer.
-
-**Cost to change later:** the bit layout is internal to the raster and the
-later slices; a change touches only `nesting::raster` and its tests.

-## #2626 - GPU stock sim S1: the f32 cut twin and the brick work list
-
-**What was decided.**
-
-1. The twin sets the f32 arithmetic that the S2 WGSL kernel must copy.
-   No WGSL exists yet, so the twin follows the f64 order of
-   `field_sweep::Sweep::dist`: the capsule closed form for the ball; for
-   the upright flat, the level closed form, the plunge closed form and a
-   32-step golden section on every other move.
-2. The tile is the brick (8 cells a side). The CPU subtracts the brick
-   origin in f64 and rounds once to f32. A cell center is
-   `(local + 0.5) * cell` in f32.
-3. The twin adds a margin to each distance before it claims:
-   `TWIN_ULPS = 32` f32 epsilons of the tile scale (reach + r + flank +
-   8 cells), plus `1e-6` of the path length on the flat path (the f64
-   golden-section bracket). The f32 cut is therefore never above the
-   f64 cut. The parity test checks this with no tolerance, because the
-   f64-to-f32 pack rounding keeps order.
-4. The max law runs on the order-preserving key (flip all bits of a
-   negative, set the sign bit of a positive). The GPU can then use an
-   unsigned atomic max.
-5. The work list uses the f64 window of each chord (`Sweep::window`),
-   clipped to the lattice box of `pack_cut`. It is made in f64 on the
-   CPU. The items are sorted brick-major, then by chord.
-6. The twin refuses, by name, every tool other than the ball and the
-   flat end mill, an arc move, a tilted axis (also for the ball) and a
-   zero-length feed move. The f64 cut accepts a zero-length move as a
-   station; the issue asks the twin to refuse it.
-7. The twin writes the cut layer only. The ray-entry layers
-   (`cut_ups`, `cut_downs`) stay out: the issue makes S1 a display
-   reference and S2 writes only the cut layer.
-8. The parity test compares values after a clamp at `-cap` on the two
-   sides. A cut under `-cap` never shows (the mesh layer is at least
-   `-cap`), and a claim that sits at the `cap` threshold on one side
-   only must compare by its visible value.
-
-**Why.** The issue asks for one-sided parity ("never more removal") and
-for a refusal by name. A margin in the kernel gives the one-sided bound
-by construction. A tolerance only in the test would not.
-
-**Dropped.** A ball on a tilted axis (easy, but the issue names upright
-tools); a direct copy of `flat_tie` (the twin is conservative on the
-tie, and the f64 tie only claims more); a public change to the f64
-kernel (the twin reads the f64 window through the crate-internal API).
-
-**Cost to change later.** If S2 needs a different f32 order, change
-`cut_twin.rs` and keep the parity tests; the margin then follows the

-## #2655 - Thread mill on a detected through hole: excuse the exit face in ThreadBore
-
-**Decided.** Add `pub exit: Option<f64>` to `ThreadBore` in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, populated as `h.through.then_some(h.floor_z)` in `crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`. In `ThreadBore::wall_radius`, alongside vertical minor-wall facets and mouth facets at or above `self.top - WALL_BAND`, excuse a facet on the hole's minor circle band when `self.exit` is `Some(exit)` and `at_exit` holds: every vertex satisfies `z <= exit + WALL_BAND`, and every vertex on the minor circle satisfies `z >= exit - WALL_BAND`. `excused` also requires `exit` (when present) to be finite and `<= top`.
-
-**Why.** On a through hole (`through: true`), `machining2d::thread_mill` extends the helix one pitch below `floor_z` so the teeth cut a full thread out the bottom exit, and the cutter spans across the plate's bottom face at `floor_z`. `ThreadBore` previously knew only `top` (`entry_z`) and excused horizontal mouth facets only at `z >= top - WALL_BAND`. Every bottom-face triangle sharing the hole's minor rim had `wall_radius` return `None`, so the solid law convicted the lead-in and helix moves crossing `floor_z` with `Gouge` ("cuts past the finish surface").
-
-Requiring `z <= exit + WALL_BAND` on all vertices and `z >= exit - WALL_BAND` on the minor-circle vertices matches flat exit faces and downward-drafted undersides while still convicting blind hole floors (`exit: None`), intermediate shelves between `exit` and `top`, lower parts or shelves below `exit - WALL_BAND`, steps reaching inside the minor circle, and cuts past the model's major cylinder.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-- Raising `floor` in `thread_mill` so the cutter never crosses `floor_z`: would leave an incomplete thread at the exit of a through hole.
-- Checking only `max z <= exit + WALL_BAND` without bounding the on-circle vertices at `exit - WALL_BAND`: would excuse a separate plate or step sitting below the threaded plate if it shared the same hole XY and minor radius.
-- Requiring all three vertices inside `[exit - WALL_BAND, exit + WALL_BAND]`: would falsely convict a bottom face drafted downward away from the hole exit.
-
-**Cost to change later.** One `Option<f64>` field on `ThreadBore` and one helper (`at_exit`) in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, populated in `crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`.

-them at the end (`contour_whole_fence.rs`). Before a band is emitted, its lead

-each side) around each ring of another band that is cut on a level this band

-must take Top Z as its first level: a lower first level bites more than one
-stepdown. So the grown ring shares the Top Z plane with the band-0 ring, and
-a lead longer than the gap between the two rings crosses the other ring at

-happens with no stock over Top Z, at the flat levels under Top Z. The only

-   tool-centreline strokes, not glyph outlines.

-   project (`crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/glyphs.rs`). The font has
-   capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph
-   is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid with cut corners. The zero has a
-   slash.
-3. `InsertText` makes the same `Sketch` entity that `ImportDxf` makes: line
-   primitives in millimetres on the layer `text`, placed on the top face of
-   the setup's stock at X, Y and an angle. `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`, the
-   project file and `get_job` work on it with no change.
-4. A character with no glyph is refused by name. A lower-case letter is not
-   written as a capital.

-

-  does not exist on `main`, and the repository holds no font file. The UI

-  font data as new dependencies. A new dependency waits for the maintainer
-  (`needs-maintainer`), and the worker brief forbids a `Cargo.toml` change.

-  centreline along a glyph outline gives hollow letters. A single-line stroke
-  gives the solid mark that a part number needs, with a v-bit or a small end
-  mill, in one pass for each stroke.
-- A skeleton computed from outlines is a new algorithm (medial axis). A
-  drawn stroke font gives the same ride mode with a table and no algorithm.
-- Sketch chaining refuses a chain that branches. The glyphs are drawn so
-  that a stroke end meets a different stroke only inside a segment. For
-  example the arms of `Y` meet on a short flat, and the stem ends in that
-  flat. `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a chain is rejected, and
-  `each_glyph_chains_with_no_rejection_at_the_extreme_heights` pins each
-  glyph. A text sketch can never hold a rejected chain.
-- A silent change of the typed text is a wrong mark on a part. A refusal by
-  name is safe.
-- On `main`, generation from the chains of a profile is refused by name
-  (`sketch_model::generation_problem`). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on
-  sketch chains, and it depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the
-  verify and the golden CL of this issue need #1869. This slice does not
-  touch those functions, so it does not conflict with that work.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- Glyph outlines from the `egui` default fonts: needs two new dependencies
-  and a decision of the maintainer. It can come later as a second font
-  source; `TextSpec` is the place for a font choice.
-- A public-domain stroke font (Hershey): the clean-room rule permits it, but
-  a data file needs a licence entry and a parser. Our own table is 47 short
-  rows.
-- Lower-case glyphs: 26 more drawings. Part numbers are capitals and digits.

-- The text string as an editable parameter of the Engrave operation: this
-  needs a new schema field and a project version step. PR #2716 also steps

-that is not zero shows `(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO -
-NO OFFSET WRITTEN)` and ends the program with `M2`. The offset is not written.
-
-```
-o903 if [[#5230 NE 0] OR [#5250 NE 0]]
-(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO - NO OFFSET WRITTEN)
-M2
-o903 endif

-  5210 + 20 x the system number: `#5230` for G54). The post cannot read it
-  at post time. Only the program can test it.
-- The rule "target = active offset + deviation" (#2610) is proved for
-  unrotated systems. With all rotations zero, the guard never fires and the
-  proof holds.

-  system have origin `a` and rotation `α`, the target rotation `τ`, the
-  machine position `m` and the deviation `d`. The write gives the target

-  With the second rule, an X deviation `d` also moves Y by `d tan(R)`.
-  Nothing here was run on a control. The Prime Directive permits a
-  visible refusal and does not permit an unproved offset.

-  unguarded, so that a rotated system can still get its Z from a probe.

-
-**Cost to change later.** If a run on LinuxCNC or PathPilot shows that

-## #2689 - A linked model's digest is of the bytes the import parsed
-
-**What was decided.**
-
-- `ImportModel::within` reads the file once
-  (`geometry/import/sourced.rs`, `load_model_open_sourced`). A buffered
-  format (OBJ, STEP, `.sc`) hashes the buffer it parses. STL keeps its
-  streaming parse (the M5.3 E law: the file never coexists with its
-  triangles) and is hashed as the stream reads it, through a reader that
-  hashes every byte it hands out. The ASCII path rewinds to byte 0 once
-  after the sniff; the rewind starts the hash again. Any other seek is
-  refused, so the digest is always of one pass. Bytes after the last
-  binary facet, if the file grew, are read into the same pass.
-- So a file that changes during the import records the digest of the
-  bytes that made the mesh. The link check then sees the newer file as
-  changed and imports it again. Before, the digest came from a second
-  read after the parse, and a change between the two reads was missed.
-- The kernel's SHA-256 takes bytes in pieces (`Sha256`, `update`,
-  `finish_hex`); `hex_digest` is that over one piece. Pinned against the
-  one-shot digest for every split around the padding edges.
-- The link check (`model_source::read`) hashes the file in 1 MiB pieces.
-  Before, it read the whole file into memory every time a linked file
-  changed, which for a large STL broke the same memory law.
-- The browser build is unchanged: it records no link.
-
-**Why.** Found in the review of #2563 (#2689). Solidcraft's Send to
-CamCraft (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936) saves the design while CamCraft
-may still be importing the previous save; that change must not be lost.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-
-- Read STL into memory like the other formats: one line, but it breaks
-  the streaming law for the largest files.
-- Compare the file's size and time before and after the parse, and
-  record no digest on a change: it would unlink the model, or need a
-  marker digest that is not a real one.
-
-**Cost to change later.** Low: one module, one kernel type; the tests in
-`crates/app/tests/model_link.rs` and `sha256.rs` pin the behaviour.

-## #2710 - The travel check judges the quarter points that an arc sweeps
-
-Date: 2026-11-19. Taken unattended by the issue worker.
-
-**What was decided**
-

-quarter point of its circle only when the sweep passes that point. The sweep
-runs from `from` to `to` in the direction of `arc.ccw`, in the arc's own
-plane. This is the same reading that `cl::plane::sweep` gives to the chords
-and that the post writes as G2/G3.
-
-The check stays strict. It keeps all four quarter points in these cases:
-
-- The in-plane endpoints are 0.01 mm apart or less (`SAME_WORD`). Their NC
-  words can be equal, and a control turns equal endpoints a full circle.
-- The sweep reads zero or is not finite (endpoints on one ray, a bad center).
-
-The radius is the larger of the two endpoint radii. The old code used the
-radius at `from`. A ramping arc (a thread ramp) can be larger at `to`, and a
-selective check must not read it smaller than it is.
-
-A quarter point within 1e-9 rad of an endpoint counts as swept
-(`ANGLE_SLACK`). No test can show this guard alone, because the endpoint
-itself is always judged. It costs nothing and it cannot hide a point.

-for XY, so the XY values do not change.

-**Why**

-A four-decimal inch post has a 0.00254 mm step on each axis. Endpoints
-less than 0.0036 mm apart can round to the same point on a diagonal.
-The 0.01 mm bound includes margin and agrees with `ring_zig::MIN_ARC_CHORD`.
-
-A shallow arc of a 22 m radius is a legal move. The old check judged points
-22 m away from the tool and refused the program on each machine size. The
-issue's reporter and the triage comment asked for the swept reading.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- A 0.001 mm endpoint bound. It misses endpoints that round to one point
-  with four-decimal inch words or three-decimal mm words.
-
-- A cap on the arc radius, or a switch to chords for large radii. Two
-  readings of one arc can disagree; the swept quarter points are exact.
-- A call to `cl::plane::sweep`. It is `pub(crate)` in `camcraft-cl`, and the
-  judge needs the start angle, which `ArcMove::radius_sweep` does not give.
-  A wider `camcraft-cl` API is not needed for six lines of angle math.

-  already passes NaN silently in the callers; that is older behaviour and a
-  separate defect, if it is one.

-more than a half turn is replaced by the other diagonal of its two facets.
-A flip is made only where the two new facets keep their winding in the
-parameter plane and the new edge passes the chord-height limit of the
-split. No point moves. No boundary edge changes. Only a face that the split
-of #2600 changed is flipped.

-  gate green, but the user still sees false edges on the wall of each bar

-  degrees stay in the mesh.

-
-**What was decided.** When the curved-face fit (`step_fit.rs`, #2600)
-cannot read a face's mesh, it returns the reason. The reasons are: no
-surface parameters, parameters that do not give the mesh's points, a facet
-that is not a triangle, a point index that the mesh does not hold, too
-many points, a tolerance that is not positive, and no surface in the shell.
-The import then:
-
-- keeps the kernel's facets of that face;
-- logs `step: face <n> keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (<reason>);
-  the model is reduced fidelity` at warn level;
-- reports the face's height as `UNMEASURED` (1000 file units). The model
-  is then reduced fidelity (#864), and verify refuses its operations.
-
-**Why.**
-
-- The issue permits two ways: measure the kept mesh, or mark the model
-  reduced fidelity. To mark it is the smaller change, and it is sound: a
-  face that was not measured is never verified as exact.
-- To measure the kept mesh needs a nearest-point search on the surface.
-  For a mesh with no parameters there is no start point for the search, and
-  truck's search on an unbounded cylinder or cone without a start point can
-  fail. A failed search then needs a second fallback.

-  micrometre to the kilometre, and under `model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`
-  (1e12 mm), so the "saved before v58" words of that sentinel do not show.

-**What was considered and dropped.**

-  now; it is the better result for a user, because a fine kernel mesh would
-  stay at full fidelity.
-- Refuse the import (an infinite chord fails at `step.rs`): too strong for
-  a model that only has one face that is not measured. Dropped.
-- Reuse the unknown-fidelity sentinel: its words say the project is old.

-  (`open failed: <path>`, `written to <path>`). The shared form now scrubs
-  the whole report text (`report_scrub::scrub_paths`): each path-like word
-  shrinks to its last component. A path starts with `/`, `\`, UNC `\\`, a drive
-  (`C:\`, `C:/`), `~`, `./` or `../`, or has a `\` or two `/`. A path runs
-  over spaces and marks to the last later word of the same line that has a
-  separator. A mark (`,`, `;`, `)`, a quote) inside a folder name does not
-  end the path (`OneDrive - Contoso, Ltd\...`). Two paths on one line merge

-  limits:
-  - A path to a folder keeps the last folder name.
-  - A relative path without a root keeps its first word when that word has
-    no separator (`jane doe/x/y` keeps `jane`).
-  - A non-path text with two `/` (for example a GPU driver text) shrinks
-    to its last part.

-## #2814 - Use available CPUs for the default gate budget
-
-**What was decided**
-
-- Use `std::thread::available_parallelism()` for the default job budget.
-  Clamp the default to 2 through 64 jobs. Use 2 if CPU detection fails.
-- Keep `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` as a positive whole-number override.
-  Apply no CPU floor or cap to an explicit override.
-- Use the CPU default for an empty value. For a bad value, print a
-  diagnostic that names the value and the chosen fallback.
-- Print the source beside the chosen budget, including in `--dry-run`.
-- Keep the existing batch and release queue split. It already allows
-  `max(1, budget / 2)` lanes. Builds, isolated tests, UI steps and clippy
-  continue to run alone with the full budget.
-- Keep `plan::J` at `"6"`. It is a marker that `budget::scale` replaces
-  when a step runs. It no longer describes the default budget.
-- Leave `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` unchanged. The merging session bumps
-  it after the process changes merge.
-
-**Why**
-
-- A fixed budget of six leaves CPUs idle on larger machines.
-- The standard library reports the CPUs available to the process and
-  needs no new dependency.
-- The floor keeps two jobs available. The cap limits automatic concurrency.
-  The override lets a runner owner choose a different limit.
-- The existing queue already scales with the budget. Changing the queue
-  would add work without changing the required behaviour.
-- Keeping the marker avoids unrelated changes to tests of raw plans.
-  The lane fixtures use an explicit budget of six to remain deterministic.
-
-**Considered and dropped**
-
-- A free-memory guard. Portable free-memory detection adds scope and may
-  need a dependency. `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` can limit a machine with little
-  memory. This optional guard can be a separate change.
-- A cap on explicit overrides. Existing runner settings must continue to
-  choose their own budget, including one job or more than 64 jobs.
-- Changes to the lane scheduler. Its limit already follows the budget.
-
-**Cost to change later**
-
-- Low. CPU selection and override parsing are in `budget::from_cpu_value`.
-  Unit tests supply CPU counts to check the fallback, floor and cap.
-  A memory guard can extend that selection without changing the queue.

-
-**What was decided**
-

-  "Performance" and "Quality" (one choice), and the switches "Ground shadow"

-  work plane".

-  two off. "Quality" sets the two on. No preset is stored. The active preset
-  is the preset whose values the switches have now. A switch changed by hand
-  leaves no preset active, and the menu cannot show a preset that the view
-  does not have.

-  saved in `view.json` (`ViewPrefs::ground_shadow`, `ambient_occlusion`).
-  An old file without the keys loads them off. The default is off, so the
-  view and the pixel snapshots of #2818 do not change.
-- Ground shadow: the model bodies are projected straight down on the floor
-  (`floor::floor_z`). The footprint is sampled on a grid of 96 nodes at
-  most, blurred two times, and drawn as blended triangles with the shade on
-  each vertex. The pass is `Pipe::GroundShadow`: after the model, before the
-  translucent stock.

-  value is the share of ten short rays over the face that meet the body
-  again, marched through a surface voxel grid of 48 cells. The pass is
-  `Pipe::FacesOccluded`: the face shader with the value on its light. The
-  values are a second vertex buffer, so the model vertex buffer and the
-  other pipelines do not change.
-- Caches (`shade_cache`, held on `State::frame_cache`): the shadow keys on
-  the facet allocation and the shown pose of each body and on the floor
-  height. The occlusion keys on the facet allocation of one body, so a moved
-  body keeps its values. A switch that is off builds nothing. Each cache has
-  a counter test.

-  there, keep their values, and their tooltip says why.

-  blending in the one wgpu pass that the two shells share. They use no
-  texture and no second render target.
-- "Look at a work plane" arms one click on an origin axis in the view. The
-  view turns to face the plane that the axis is normal to: Z gives XY, X
-  gives YZ, Y gives ZX. A click on the origin point gives the XY plane. The
-  origins are the work offsets (WCS) and the world origin. The reversed axes
-  of a WCS (#1720) are applied. The view does not pan or zoom. A miss
-  changes nothing and says so.

-  change and cached. Baked vertex values and a baked shadow mesh are that

-## #2849 - The corner check reads a cusp loop that crosses itself by the even-odd rule
-
-**What was decided.** `connected_pieces` in
-`crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` builds the fill of each outer
-loop with `Region::from_slices`, not `Region::new`. A loop that crosses
-itself is read as its even-odd lobes. The corner check then runs and applies
-its usual noise filters (`PIECE_AREA_MIN`, `SLIVER_HALF_WIDTH`,
-`CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`).
-
-**Why.** The loops that `connected_pieces` reads are the output of a
-boolean (`piece.difference(&swept)`), not sketch input. A bore drawn as
-chords less its own swept area leaves a cusp a few microns wide at each
-chord vertex. On the micron lattice, the boolean can return such a cusp as
-one loop that crosses itself. `Region::new` refuses that loop, so the whole
-corner check stopped with the note "the check for corners of the stock
-tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself)".
-The refusal in `Region::new` is for ambiguous user geometry. It has no
-purpose for a noise cusp that the next filter drops. A loop that does not
-cross itself gives the same region from the two constructors.
-
-The defect does not need the solidcore importer. A synthetic 25 mm bore
-shows it on `main`: in a sweep of 24 to 400 chords, 9 tool sizes and 4
-phases, 4726 of 13572 cases stopped with the error. With the fix, no case
-stops.
-
-**Scope: partial.** The issue names three toolpath tests. The owner's
-diagnosis on the issue says that each has its own cause (the pass start
-choice, `axis_reseat`, the ring order) and that this fix does not change
-them. Their `known-fail #2849` markers are on the unpushed PR B of #917.
-This PR therefore ends with `Refs #2849`, not `Fixes #2849`.
-
-**Merge with main.** `main` got the same code fix in `bc5daa32d`
-(`outer_fills`, pinned by a hand-made bow-tie loop). The refresh takes
-main's code. This PR now adds only the chord-bore pin: it reads the real
-path (a bore less its swept area) through `unreached_corners` and
-`unreached_corner_note`, where main's pin reads `outer_fills` alone.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-- Relax `Region::new` itself. Dropped: the refusal protects sketch input
-  (Prime Directive), and many callers rely on it.
-- Skip a loop that fails `Region::new`. Dropped: that hides a loop without
-  a look at its size. The even-odd reading keeps the area and lets the
-  existing filters decide.
-- Raise `PIECE_AREA_MIN` above the cusp area. Dropped: the filter runs
-  after the constructor, and a threshold tuned to one mesh breaks with the
-  next mesh.
-- Change the planners for tests 1 to 3 (start choice, reseat tolerance,
-  ring order). Dropped here: they cannot fail on `main`, and other pins and
-  goldens read that behaviour.
-
-- Close this PR as superseded. Dropped for now: the chord-bore pin covers
-  the full corner check, not only the fill constructor. The re-review
-  decides if that coverage is worth the test.
-
-**Cost to change later.** One line. The pin
-`a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` fails if

-## #2855 - Catalog metadata and operation example links
-
-**Decided.** Each catalog case has a required `case.toml`. `kinds` uses the
-canonical display names read from the bounded `KindInfo::ALL` source table.
-`machine` and `expect` are required descriptive strings, not executable checks.

-arrays. It refuses escapes, unsupported syntax, duplicate or empty values,
-unknown fields and unknown kinds.
-
-Every known operation-kind heading gets a deterministic marked Example cases
-block, including a placeholder when no case exists. Turning headings use an
-explicit alias map where their prose titles differ from registry names. Links
-point to the canonical GitHub source folder for each case. The generator
-preserves surrounding prose and refuses malformed blocks or missing headings
-before writing partial guide updates.
-
-Metadata and links are checked across the whole catalog even with `--case`.
-The default and rebuild commands regenerate the lists. Screenshot-only and
-PDF-only commands leave the guide unchanged. `--check` validates the metadata
-and links without writing, before building the CLI. Existing NC rebuilding and
-byte-for-byte parity checks stay unchanged.
-
-**Why.** A separate metadata file keeps case READMEs readable and gives the
-catalog one source for guide links. Reading the registry source avoids a second
-kind list and an app dependency in the small process tool. Early diagnostics
-name metadata and link problems before an expensive CLI build. Validating all
-links avoids making a filtered case command silently accept broken guide pages.
-
-**Considered and dropped.** Embedding machine-readable fields in READMEs would
-mix prose with tooling input. A new app dependency or TOML dependency would
-change Cargo dependencies for a small flat schema. A separate links-only CLI
-would add another workflow when the existing catalog commands can generate and
-check the lists. Treating `machine` or `expect` as executable assertions would
-duplicate the build script and its verification checks.
-
-**Cost to change later.** The metadata reader, guide generator and turning alias
-map are isolated in xtask. Supporting richer TOML later requires extending or
-replacing the reader and its tests; existing flat metadata remains valid.
-Changing link destinations requires regenerating the marked guide blocks.

-  2. Refuse G76 by name in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`g76Why`) whenever `p.StartInAir !== true`, so a start point above material (or a cached pre-#2878 record or legacy stream without `AIR 1`) never writes a G76 cycle.
-  3. -  4. Allow `turning::thread` to extend `k_hi` up to `top_z` past the bar's free end face and fix `revolve::lattice` not to re-push out-of-domain window endpoints after `lat.retain`, so a G76 thread can start in free air in front of the end face.

-
-- **Why**:
-  - A Fanuc-type G76 moves the insert from the start point to each pass's depth at rapid traverse. Checking `StockZTop` alone in `.cps` cannot distinguish a faced end or a machined relief groove from uncut stock, nor does the post script know the insert width or part silhouette. Computing `start_in_air` from the revolved part, stock and prior cuts in the generator/verifier and requiring `StartInAir === true` in `fanuc-lathe.cps` is fail-safe by default: older caches and hand-written streams without `AIR 1` refuse G76 rather than silently rapiding into steel, while G32 passes (which plunge with `G01`) stay unchanged.
-  - Putting the `StartInAir` check at the end of `g76Why` preserves more specific plan/range/hand refusals (such as chip-break dips or alternating flank infeed).
-

-  - **Checking only `StockZTop` inside `fanuc-lathe.cps`**: dropped because it rejects valid relief grooves and faced bars (where `start.z < StockZTop`) and misses narrow end-face overlaps where `start.z > StockZTop` but `start.z - insert_width/2 < StockZTop`, as well as flank-infeed shifts.
-  - **Auto-shifting the G76 start point inside `fanuc-lathe.cps`**: dropped because the post never shifts verified points (`fanuc-lathe.cps` law) and shifting past a solid bar would cut unmodeled length.

-- **Decided:**
-  1. Remove the post-filter re-insertion of `window`'s endpoints `(w0, w1)` in `revolve::lattice` (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`). Every endpoint inside the bar domain `[d_lo, d_hi]` is already in `lat` from each move's `raw_band`; dropping the re-insertion keeps `lat` strictly inside `[d_lo, d_hi]` as the module's domain law states.
-  2. In `thread_planned_in` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`), compute `k_hi` from the unclamped `f.station_of(p.top_z)` instead of `blade::setup`'s clamped `s_hi`, while keeping `s_lo..=s_hi` clamped for `ref_top`, valley phase discovery, and the empty-window refusal. The same change landed on `main` first in #2892 (#2878) in the form `let s_hi_pass = f.station_of(p.top_z).max(s_hi);`. Because `blade::setup` sets `s_hi = f.station_of(top_z).min(d_hi)`, `s_hi <= station_of(top_z)` always and the two forms give the same value. The merge of `main` into this branch kept main's `s_hi_pass` form; this PR now adds the pinning tests of `turning_thread_end_face`, which also guard the #2892 fix.
-
-- **Why:**
-  - Re-inserting `w0` and `w1` after `lat.retain(|s| (d_lo..=d_hi).contains(s))` added intervals outside the bar whenever a move's band extended past an end face (by 0.1 mm on a free-end groove, by full pitches on a free-air lead-in, or by half a blade width on a free-end groove). In those air intervals `E(s) = 0`, so `revolve::scan` reported the capped wave floor (or blade tip) as rest and blocked the post.
-  - Because `blade::setup` clamps `s_hi` to `d_hi`, setting `top_z` in front of the end face could never place lead-in lattice points in free air; every pass still started inside the part. -## #2882 - Thin turning profile samples that are closer than half the chord share
-
-**What was decided:**
-- Add a private `thin` step in `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`.
-- `thin` drops each sample that lies closer than `MIN_GAP_SHARE * share` to the last kept sample. `MIN_GAP_SHARE` is `0.5`.
-- `thin` always keeps the first sample and the last sample. The window ends stay.
-- `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in` both run the outside ride and the inside ride through `thin`.
-
-**Why:**
-- Near a vertical tangent of the offset curve, the chord bisection places samples less than 1 micrometre apart. The lathe posts then write runs of identical G01 blocks. The Fanuc example wrote 408 identical blocks in one cone-thread program.
-- `out.dedup()` removes only exact duplicates, so it does not fix this case.
-- Thinning at the source fixes every turning ride. This covers profile rough, profile finish, contour and boring. It also covers every lathe post.
-- Each kept sample is still an exact point of the offset curve. No kept sample gouges.
-- Each dropped sample lies within the gap of a kept sample. At the window end, a kept sample can give way to the last sample, so a dropped sample lies within two gaps of a kept one. A chord therefore moves by at most two gaps. The chord bound becomes `2 * share`.
-- The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share. The ride therefore stays within half of the user tolerance.
-- At a tolerance of 0.01 mm, the share is 0.0025 mm. The least gap is then 0.00125 mm. That gap is more than the posted resolution of 0.001 mm.
-
-**What was considered and dropped:**
-- Drop repeated feed blocks in each lathe post (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`), when a block has the same words as the last block.
-  - Dropped because it hides the cause in each post.
-  - Dropped because it changes posted output in two dialects.
-  - Dropped because the project file still keeps the dense samples.
-- Use a fixed absolute gap, for example 1 micrometre.
-  - Dropped because a fixed gap does not scale with the tolerance that the user sets.
-
-**Cost to change later:**
-- Low. The change is one private function and one constant in `offset.rs`. The pinning test is `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`.
-- Changing `MIN_GAP_SHARE` changes the chord bound. Keep the bound at `2 * share`, or update the tolerance claim in this entry.
-- Known limit: at a very small user tolerance, for example 0.001 mm, the gap is below the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This is rare and it costs no position.

-change uses that public API and does not change entity references or
-parameters.

-The authored fixtures `testdata/models/short_units_inch.step` and
-`testdata/models/short_units_metre.step` use our unit-box geometry. The
-regression tests check the imported dimensions, volume, and declared units.

-of every short-name file would reject legal files that the existing unit
-reader can handle after name expansion. A dependency update would widen

-**What was decided (review of PR #2927):** The model read
-(`camcraft_kernel::step_length_units`) refuses by name:
-
-- a file with a length unit when no unit context states a length unit
-  (the same rule as the tool-body read, `camcraft_geometry::step_units`);

-  a different context of the file states one;

-## #2958 - Viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
-
-**What was decided.**
-
-- The viewport overlay draws as screen-facing quads, one 32-byte instance for each segment (two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours). The vertex shader makes the six corners. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over one pixel. The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed.
-- The overlay includes toolpaths, height planes, region outlines, triads, the ground grid and the other overlay lines. All of these use the one width.
-- The default width is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the display's pixels per point. The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt.
-- Each wide-line vertex moves toward the eye by `LIFT_WIDTHS` = 3 line widths of world distance. The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection.
-- Each end of a line extends half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet thus close the corner and do not overlap past it.
-- MSAA is a setting: Off, 2x or 4x. The default is 4x. All the viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound.
-- The windowed shell requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it, and reads the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts (1 and 4) are offered. The browser build always offers only 1 and 4.
-- An anti-aliasing entry for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A pick of such a count is refused by name.
-- A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so once.
-- The two settings are per-user view settings in `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. They are not in `prefs.json`. They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme.
-- The two settings are in the viewport's Display menu (#2818), in its Graphics group, after the projection. They were first in the Theme door. A manual test found that place wrong: line width and anti-aliasing are not part of a theme. #2818 had added the Display menu with a Graphics group, so they moved there. A general Settings window is proposed in #3025.
-- Like the other Display menu entries, a pick is a direct `State` method call (`select_line_width`, `select_antialias`), not a queued command.
-
-**Why.**
-
-- A `wgpu` line is always one hardware pixel wide and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths were hard to see next to the 3 px egui triad (#195).
-- 2 pt and more made the dense paths into one solid area when the camera is far. Thus the default is 1.5 pt.
-- Without the lift, half of a wide line that lies on a face failed the depth test. In the pinning test, 292 px were visible on the face against 628 px for the same line in the air.
-- An instanced segment uses 32 bytes against 48 for the old vertex pair. At the overlay limit (512k segments) this is 16 MiB against 24 MiB.
-- For the fallback, a lower count never uses more memory than the user asked for.
-- `view.json` already holds the viewport's look (the origin names). `prefs.json` was already past the 400-line file limit.
-
-**Considered and dropped.**
-
-- Draw the paths with the egui painter, as the triad is drawn. This loses the depth test and is slow on large toolpaths.
-- Six full vertices for each segment (the trial). This needed approximately 135 MB at the overlay limit.
-- A per-line width class for the ground grid. The grid already fades at its rim, so it uses the one width. This can be added later with a byte in the instance colour.
-- A fallback to a higher sample count. This uses more memory than the user asked for.
-
-**Cost to change later.**
-
-- The width and the lift are uniforms and constants in `viewport/wide.rs`.
-- A new sample count is one row in `Antialias` and one check in `offered_samples`.
-- The file words are `"1"`, `"1.5"`, `"2"`, `"3"` and `"Off"`, `"2x"`, `"4x"`. A word that the build does not know reads as the default.

-## #2965 - The first traverse of the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds
-
-- **What was decided** (issue worker, unattended; the maintainer can change it):
-  1. **The post order is the basis.** After a tool change the post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the full block with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `xyFirst` and `onRapid`). So the X/Y traverse runs before the rotaries move to the pose of the operation. The rotaries stand at a pose that the operation does not state. The Z of that traverse is the higher of the operation's clearance height and the start (`traverseZ`). The #2965 kinds are read at that height: a rotary or multi-axis path opens at its own pose (for example a radial clearance beside a standing bar, at Z -10), and the post does not traverse there. The #2901 kinds keep their reading of the start (their start is on the clearance plane, and the start is never higher than the traverse, so that reading is the stricter one).
-  2. **Rotary kinds** (`Mode::Rotary`: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset). A new law, `sim::verify::first_traverse_low_swept`, reads the work as swept through a full turn about its fitted axis:
-     - The start stock's and the part's points are read at their swept top (`swept_top`: the foot on the axis plus the radius, scaled by `sqrt(1 - dz^2)`). A 40 x 40 bar on a horizontal axis reads 28.284 over the axis, not its upright top of 20.
-     - The steel that turns with the part (`Workholding::turning`, a chuck) is read swept too, at its corners (the distance to a line is convex, so the maximum is at a corner). The steel that stands still (`Workholding::fixed`, the table, a tailstock) is read at its top in the machine frame.
-     - The start's machine height is `origin.z + t . (start - origin)`, with `t` the tool axis of move 0 (`+Z` when the move states none; the frame's axis for a 3+2 path). The machine stands the tool upright by a turn about the axis line. That turn keeps the line and maps `t` onto `+Z`. A radial start reads its radius over the axis line. When no turn about the axis stands the tool upright (a live tool beside a C axis, `stamp_spindle_c`), the start is read at the lowest height that the turn can carry it to: its own Z for a vertical C axis.
-     - Which law reads a rotary kind depends on the mounted machine (`AxisLimits::turns_part` of its tilting rotaries). Each one turns the part: the swept law only (the post writes machine heights). Each one rides the head: the tip law of item 3 only (the work never turns, and an RTCP post writes the tip in the part frame). No machine, a mixed machine, or a rotary that an old file never stated: both laws, and the first verdict is kept.
-     - The verdict is the same `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` (blocking, MCP `first_traverse_low`), so the post gate, the UI, MCP and the warned moves need no change.
-     - The axis is the job's (`fixture::rotary_axis_of`). When the job states none (a stock or selection source), the same fit of the same facets that the generator ran is used. If no axis can be fitted, generation is refused by name ("no rotary axis can be fitted to the part, so its first traverse cannot be judged"). The generator itself fits that axis, so this refusal is not expected in use.
-  3. **Multi-axis kinds** (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour). They answer to the #2901 law on their tip, upright in the part frame (or along the plane's axis in a 3+2 frame). Reason: the post writes the tip in the part frame, so the Z move and the X/Y traverse run on the part's own plane at the start height. The tool leans up from its tip in each pose that cuts from above, so the stock and the fixtures under that plane are under the whole tool.
-  4. **Cross drill on a mill** (`OpParams::Drill` with a `cross` list). Generation refuses it by name before any move ("cross holes are live-tooling work - the mounted machine is a mill with no turret"), so it can have no first traverse. The test pins that refusal. The selection still includes the kind, so the tip law reads it if a mill ever generates radial holes.
-  5. **Cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn** (`Kind::Lathe`, `Kind::MillTurn`, live tooling) is not judged by this law. `is_mill` is false there, as for the turning kinds of #2901. A lathe turret does not traverse in a mill's X/Y plane. Its radial approach is judged by the cross-drill standoff (`cross_stock::standoff`, the raw stock radius) and the rapid laws. This decision records that limit; it is not proof that the lathe approach has no collision. #3077 owns that gap.
-- **Cache.** The post gate trusts the verdicts that a cache carries. The op stamp of the multi-axis kinds, the rotary kinds and the cross drill (`first_traverse::newly_judged`) takes one more word, `first-traverse-2965`. Such a cache reads Stale once and the post refuses it until a regenerate. The salt `camcraft-op-stamp-v4` does not change, so no other kind's stamp moves and the pinned stamps (`deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`) stay. Dropped: a salt v5 for all kinds (each saved cache and each pinned stamp moves, for kinds whose law did not change).
-- **Example projects (the maintainer accepted: regenerate, stamp only).** The new stamp word makes two committed projects read Stale once. They are regenerated, as #2901 regenerated its four examples. The diff is the operation stamp fields only, and each `.nc` and golden stays byte-identical:
-  - `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` (operation `Journal`, a continuous 4-axis kind): by its own test, `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part`. That run also rewrote `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` with a last-digit change in seven A words (for example `A-54.14` -> `A-54.141`). That change was discarded: the suite passes (10/10) with the committed `.nc` and the new project, so the program stays byte-identical.
-  - `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (operation `Swarf1`): loaded, `Swarf1` regenerated with `GenerateOperation`, saved with `project::save` (the #2901 path). Its own path, `cargo xtask docs-images`, builds all three guide projects again and renders the guide images, which changes more than the stamp; it was not used. `Indexed Face1` (a face, not a #2965 kind) keeps its stamp.
-- **Pinning tests.** `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_rotary.rs`: `a_rotary_kind_reads_its_square_bar_swept_about_the_axis`, `a_5_axis_kind_reads_a_far_clamp_over_its_clearance_plane`, `a_cross_drill_on_a_mill_is_refused_before_any_traverse`. The sim unit tests in `crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse.rs` pin the swept law (corner radius, radial start, chuck and tailstock, axis tilt, a C axis, the clearance height).
-- **Why one law per frame and no new verdict.** The #2901 verdict already blocks the post, carries its two heights and has its UI, MCP and warned-move mappings. A new variant would add four mappings and no new information. The words "clearance height Z..." read the machine height over the axis for a rotary kind, which is the clearance radius when the axis is at Z 0.
-- **Known limits.**
-  - A machine with two rotaries: the rotary kinds read the sweep about the one fitted axis only. The multi-axis kinds read the tip in the part frame; a pose that leans the tool down from its tip (an undercut) is not read.
-  - The tool radius is not added: the law reads the tip, as the #2901 law does. A horizontal tool (cross drill) can reach one radius under its tip line.
-- **What was considered and dropped**:
-  - The rotary kinds read at the start angle only (no sweep): wrong, because the rotary words come after the X/Y traverse.
-  - A sweep for the multi-axis kinds about each machine rotary: the machine's axis lines are not stated in the part frame for those kinds (`rotary_axis_of` is `None` for them), so the sweep has no line to turn about.
-  - A refusal of every multi-axis and cross-drill operation (no law, only a refusal): it blocks programs that the tip law shows to be safe.
-  - The judge in `camcraft-motion`: the verdict and the steel types are in `camcraft-sim`, as for #2901. No crate edge is added.
-- **Cost to change later**: low. One law function and the selection in `operation::first_traverse` (`answers`, `turned_axis`).
